+status=source_derived_unreviewed; committed Ultra source 788beab, selected exact bytes preserved in FM. Internal conditional derivations and model counterexamples; no acquired repair capability, external correctness review, historical novelty clearance or matched complete-cost advantage.
+
+Task: choose a durable repair process for fatigue-relevant pores in additive-manufactured metal when a CT-visible cavity may connect to the surface through an unresolved throat. The decision output is qualified bonding, regrowth/fatigue or functional-leak outcome under a feasible process, not merely CT pore disappearance. Existing studies report surface-connected pore and regrowth problems in their material/process scopes. N702 treats electrically shielded CLOSED powder cavities through a distinct polarizability/mass interface and expressly supplies no open-pore or printed-part-integrity bound; no mathematical transfer from N702 is asserted here.
+
+Under the source's ideal-gas, cylindrical continuum no-slip, quasi-steady common-temperature assumptions, P is external and p internal absolute pressure, V is cavity volume, a and L are throat radius and length, T temperature, and mu viscosity. With n=pV/(RT) and C=pi*a^4/(16*mu*L*V), the source derives n'=pi*a^4*(P^2-p^2)/(16*mu*L*R*T), p'=C*(P^2-p^2)+p*(T'/T-V'/V), and, for P>0, q'=C*P*(1-q^2)+(c+theta-r)*q for q=p/P, c=-V'/V, theta=T'/T, r=P'/P. These are conditional conservation equations, not acquired hot-metal transport laws. Evolving conductance, gas regime, material deformation and contact must be measured.
+
+The internally derived slew exclusion has exact initial-condition scope. If P>=0 is nondecreasing, P'<=R_max, p>=0, C(t)>=C_min>0 and c+theta>=0 throughout an acquired interval, then Delta=P-p obeys Delta(t)<=max{Delta(0),sqrt(R_max/C_min)}. It excludes a declared minimum pressure deficit only while the evolving conductance lower bound remains valid; it neither rules out slow subthreshold creep nor capillary/chemical closure. A genuinely sealed cavity with no gas loss obeys p_f=p_s*(V_s/V_f)*(T_f/T_s); without other inward traction the necessary quasistatic balance is p_s/P_f<=(V_f/V_s)*(T_s/T_f). A finite positive throat radius does not constitute a gas-tight seal.
+
+The decisive source countermodel holds the entire room-temperature tracer map fixed and changes only unmeasured hot creep. In its dimensionless restricted model P=1, V fixed, p'=exp(-4z)*(1-p), z'=m*(1-p), z=ln(a0/a). At a geometric criterion z=ln 2, m=10 reaches p=3/128; m=1/10 stalls before the criterion. A separate full compressible-flow construction also separates hot geometric outcomes while retaining the same room map. These are constructed model worlds, not measured alloy pairs. Literal sealing requires an additional contact, snap or bonding law. More exact cold inversion alone cannot decide the hot action under the stated information interface.
+
+For a proposed isotope-labelled HIP coupon assay, the calibrated two-source relation f=(1-lambda)*f0+lambda*fH identifies the RETAINED fraction lambda from HIP-source gas when effective endmembers, fractionation, blanks and extraction bias have acquired bounds. It does not identify net uptake or seal time. In the exact three-isotope counterexample, positive ingress measures (4/7)delta_(1/4)+(3/7)delta_(5/6) and (1/6)delta_0+(2/3)delta_(1/2)+(1/6)delta_1 have equal total mass, mean 1/2, second moment 1/3 and identical isotope counts for the source's valid time code, but last ingress times 5/6 and 1. An exchange construction likewise has identical total gas and final isotope fraction with distinct cutoffs. A null late marker excludes an open path only after acquiring a lower bound on hot open-path uptake.
+
+Generic rapid closure before gas ingress is disclosed by pneumatic isostatic forging (EP1024911B1 / US5816090A); generic isotope-tagged HIP gas plus post-treatment mass spectrometry is disclosed in EP3243585A1. Curvature-selective deposition is established in other materials, without an acquired alloy-compatible hermetic plug that survives HIP and preserves bonding/fatigue. These disclosures preempt the generic novelty claims; they do not prove the particular AM-metal assay or repair outcome. Public morphology data supplied 17,222 pre-HIP pore rows in one parsed sample, but lacked throat conductance, hot connectivity, paired process actions and bonding/fatigue labels. A restricted same-data optimizer could select the same schedule. Internal arithmetic/replays and source checks have only their recorded bounded scope.
+
+Decision: preserve the pressure and isotope countermodels and abandon generic rapid-ramp, Kelvin-deposition and isotope-coding novelty claims. A CT-registered source-resolved pore assay remains an unperformed small-coupon hypothesis. Its decisive controls are known sealed/open/throttled cavities, blind registered gas recovery, acquired endmember/blank/fractionation and hot transport, matched qualified HIP, rapid forging and verified preseal arms, then bonding, regrowth, fatigue/leak and complete-resource measurements. UNKNOWN remains appropriate until those interfaces are acquired. No civilization-enabling capability is established.

A small infeasible dual residual cannot by itself certify an upper bound: a component delta in a mode of eigenvalue epsilon can add delta^2/epsilon. Require exact frustration-free checks L_j psi=0, Z>0 and a local Hermitian V for the physical curvature interpretation. For each physical row j, choose finite operators O_(j,a) whose support interval contains supp(L_j*L_j), and set w_j=sum_a c_(j,a)L_j O_(j,a)psi. Let columns of A be a_(j,a)=L_j*L_j O_(j,a)psi. Compute transfer-contracted K=A*A, g=A*b, h=<b,b> and physical row metric M_(j,a),(k,b)=delta_(j,k)<L_j O_(j,a)psi,L_j O_(j,b)psi>. Solve Kc0=g and rho=h-g*c0=||b-Ac0||^2. If rho!=0, this dictionary fails and the operation returns UNKNOWN. If rho=0, minimize c*Mc over c=c0+Tz, where columns of T span ker K, by the exact reduced equation (T*MT)z=-T*Mc0, after exact row-dependency removal or quotient. The resulting c, transfer contractions, equality Ac=b and norm c*Mc/Z provide an exactly checkable upper witness. M is neither K nor the identity: overlapping dictionary placements on the SAME physical bond have cross terms and must be merged before charging the bond norm. An initial numerical probe split those physical rows and spuriously halved the norm; all reported exact uppers use corrected M.

+Locality and cost scope. Frustration freedom and disjoint supports make K block banded: if supp(L_i*L_i) is disjoint from supp O_(j,b), then (L_i*L_i)(L_j*L_j)O_(j,b)psi=0. Similarly g has source-near support, while M is block diagonal by physical rows. No gap, exponential clustering or inverse transfer is needed for these zero identities. Coefficients and null vectors can nevertheless extend across the chain. Exact MPS contractions and rational linear algebra have polynomial bit cost in N and input bit length for fixed d,D,R,s; the dense coefficient solve is polynomial, not claimed linear time. +--- BEGIN SOURCE BYTES ---
+## Conservation before and after sealing
+
+Under ideal-gas, cylindrical, continuum, no-slip, quasi-steady, common-temperature assumptions, let external and internal absolute pressures be P and p, cavity volume V, throat radius a and length L, gas temperature T and viscosity mu. Write n=pV/(RT). Then
+
+    dn/dt = pi a^4 (P^2-p^2)/(16 mu L R T)
+    dp/dt = C(P^2-p^2) + p(T'/T - V'/V)
+    C = pi a^4/(16 mu L V).
+
+For q=p/P, c=-V'/V, theta=T'/T and r=P'/P,
+
+    q' = CP(1-q^2) + (c+theta-r)q.
+
+Shrinking the cavity and heating its gas increase internal pressure. Narrowing the throat decreases gas conductance. Neither effect can be dropped silently. These equations are conditional fluid mechanics, not a new physical law. Slip/Knudsen flow, nonideal gas, evolving complex throats, adsorption and gas dissolution require different or measured transport laws.
+
+After a genuinely gas-tight seal and with no dissolution/diffusion, n is fixed. At prescribed final temperature, p_f=p_s(V_s/V_f)(T_f/T_s). Without capillary or other closing traction, ongoing pressure-driven contraction to V_f requires
+
+    p_s/P_f <= (V_f/V_s)(T_s/T_f).
+
+If additional inward traction is bounded by Pi_max, replace P_f with P_f+Pi_max. This is a necessary quasistatic pressure-balance gate, not a universal volume floor in the presence of capillarity, plastic overshoot, gas loss or bonding. An adiabatic sealed gas has a different relation, pV^gamma=constant. CT disappearance alone does not establish a seal, diffusion bond, fatigue improvement or absence of regrowth.
+
+## A conservative pressure-slew exclusion certificate
+
+Suppose P>=0 is nondecreasing and absolutely continuous, P'<=R_max, p>=0, C(t)>=C_min>0, and c+theta>=0 on an acquired interval. Let Delta=P-p with Delta(0)<=D. At a putative first crossing Delta=D, necessarily P>=D and
+
+    Delta' = P' - C D(2P-D) - (c+theta)p
+           <= R_max - C_min D^2.
+
+Hence, by scalar comparison (or a strict barrier followed by a limit), if R_max<=C_min D^2, Delta(t)<=D throughout the interval. In general Delta<=max{Delta(0),sqrt(R_max/C_min)}. This excludes attaining a declared minimum pressure deficit if the coefficient bound remains valid. It does NOT rule out arbitrarily slow below-threshold creep or independent capillary/chemical sealing. If a throat law has no deformation below an independently measured threshold Y>D, it excludes pressure-induced throat sealing over that interval. If a finite-time creep upper bound is instead supplied, integrate that upper bound and compare with the required closure strain. A throat may reduce C as it closes; an initial C alone is insufficient for the certificate.
+
+The fourth-root critical-radius expression under constant geometry is
+
+    a_critical = [16 mu L V R_max/(pi D^2)]^(1/4).
+
+With fixed acquired geometry, a>=a_critical makes the slew bound at most D (provided the initial deficit is at most D). It is a sensitivity expression, not a numerical prediction for an alloy. The public sources do not provide the complete hot throat geometry, constitutive law and gas-property uncertainty needed to evaluate a physical certificate.

+## What a normalized contrast-gas query actually acquires
+
+For a fixed cavity, constant external step P_x, initial p=0 and fixed coefficient C_x,
+
+    p(t)/P_x = tanh(C_x P_x t).
+
+Suppose attenuation is y=b+s p/T_x. If the baseline y_0 and fully equilibrated y_inf are independently obtained without changing the cavity, normalized u=(y-y_0)/(y_inf-y_0) cancels b,s and gives p/P_x. An error bound epsilon on the ENTIRE normalized reading gives
+
+    atanh(max(0,u-epsilon))/(P_x t) <= C_x
+      <= atanh(min(1,u+epsilon))/(P_x t),
+
+with infinite upper endpoint when u+epsilon>=1. A missing response after finite time bounds transport; it does not prove isolation. Acquiring the equilibrium normalization of an almost isolated cavity may itself take prohibitively long. It must be replaced by an independently calibrated contrast/volume scale, with its errors charged. Mixtures of cavities, changing geometry and adsorption do not inherit the single-cavity formula.
+
+A hot coefficient interval requires an acquired transfer factor
+
+    C_H/C_x = (a_H/a_x)^4 (mu_x/mu_H) (L_x/L_H) (V_x/V_H)
+
+in this model, as well as the hot closure law. Without those inputs, the implementation returns UNKNOWN. Standard nonlinear fitting or c-optimal design given the identical observations has access to the identical coefficient interval; this is not an advantage over an equally informed method.
+
+## Exact action-changing ambiguity survives a perfect room tracer
+
+Two model worlds have identical geometry, gas laws and all room-temperature tracer observations. Give them different unmeasured hot throat creep coefficients m. In a restricted dimensionless hot model at P=1, fixed V, z=ln(a0/a),
+
+    p'=exp(-4z)(1-p),   z'=m(1-p),   geometric criterion at z=ln 2.
+
+Eliminating time gives p(z)=(1-exp(-4z))/(4m). For m=10, pressure at the criterion is 3/128. For m=1/10, the formal criterion pressure is 75/32>1; the trajectory stalls at z=-ln(3/5)/4<ln2. One world reaches the stipulated geometric criterion with a low gas inventory; the other cannot. A finite z means a POSITIVE cylindrical radius; a gas-tight seal needs an additional independently acquired contact, snap-through or bonding law at that event. The ODE alone does not supply a seal. The equality of the two complete room tracer maps is by construction, not a claim about an experimentally discovered alloy pair.
+
+The obstruction also survives full compressible Poiseuille flow. Let q'=tau^-1 exp(-4z)(1-q^2), z'=lambda(1-q), with q(0)=z(0)=0. Then
+
+    ln(1+q)=(1-exp(-4z))/(4 lambda tau).
+
+At z_s=0.1, lambda*tau=0.2 reaches the geometric criterion at q about 0.51; lambda*tau=0.01 approaches q=1 before that criterion. These worlds can share the same full room map. Literal sealing again needs the additional contact/bond law. Thus more accurate room imaging or room transient fitting cannot acquire the missing hot state-to-action link without a validated transfer or hot test.

+#!/usr/bin/env python3
+"""Compact exact Gram feasibility for local AKLT susceptibility duals.
+
+No 3**N vector or matrix is constructed. Each local column is a three-site
+rank-one operator acting on the integer-gauge AKLT MPS. Gram entries use 4x4
+transfer matrices and exact signed integers after scaling each column by 6.
+Only bond separations 0, 1, and 2 can contribute to the Gram matrix.
+"""
+
+from dataclasses import dataclass
+import json
+from pathlib import Path
+import sys
+
+import numpy as np
+import sympy as sp
+from sympy.polys.matrices import DomainMatrix
+
+
+N = int(sys.argv[1]) if len(sys.argv) > 1 else 6
+assert N >= 6
+A = (
+    np.array([[0, 2], [0, 0]], dtype=object),
+    np.array([[-1, 0], [0, 1]], dtype=object),
+    np.array([[0, 0], [-1, 0]], dtype=object),
+)
+I2 = np.eye(2, dtype=object)
+E = sum((np.kron(a, a) for a in A), np.zeros((4, 4), dtype=object))
+MAG = (1, 0, -1)
+PAIR_BASIS = ((0, 0), (0, 1), (0, 2), (1, 2), (2, 2))
+V_BASIS = ((0, 1, 1), (0, 1, 2), (1, 1, 1), (1, 1, 2))
+Q6 = {
+    (0, 0): {(0, 0): 6},
+    (0, 1): {(0, 1): 3, (1, 0): 3},
+    (0, 2): {(0, 2): 1, (1, 1): 2, (2, 0): 1},
+    (1, 2): {(1, 2): 3, (2, 1): 3},
+    (2, 2): {(2, 2): 6},
+}
+
+
+@dataclass(frozen=True)
+class Defect:
+    sites: tuple[int, ...]
+    q6: dict[tuple[int, ...], int]
+    c: np.ndarray
+
+
+def dual(bond, offset, u, v):
+    sites = tuple((bond + offset + t) % N for t in range(3))
+    pair_pos = -offset
+    q6 = {}
+    for pair, coeff in Q6[u[pair_pos:pair_pos + 2]].items():
+        word = list(u)
+        word[pair_pos:pair_pos + 2] = pair
+        q6[tuple(word)] = coeff
+    c = A[v[0]] @ A[v[1]] @ A[v[2]]
+    return Defect(sites, q6, c)
+
+
+def source():
+    return (
+        Defect((0,), {(0,): 6}, A[0]),
+        Defect((0,), {(2,): -6}, A[2]),
+    )
+
+
+def local_basis(bond):
+    out = []
+    for offset in (0, -1):
+        for v in V_BASIS:
+            mv = sum(MAG[t] for t in v)
+            for pair in PAIR_BASIS:
+                for spectator in range(3):
+                    u = (*pair, spectator) if offset == 0 else (spectator, *pair)
+                    if sum(MAG[t] for t in u) == mv:
+                        out.append(dual(bond, offset, u, v))
+    assert len(out) == 24
+    return out
+
+
+def overlap(left, right):
+    """Exact overlap of *six-times-scaled* states via 4x4 transfers."""
+    if isinstance(left, tuple):
+        return sum(overlap(item, right) for item in left)
+    if isinstance(right, tuple):
+        return sum(overlap(left, item) for item in right)
+    lp = {site: p for p, site in enumerate(left.sites)}
+    rp = {site: p for p, site in enumerate(right.sites)}
+    total = 0
+    for lw, lc in left.q6.items():
+        for rw, rc in right.q6.items():
+            product = np.eye(4, dtype=object)
+            compatible = True
+            for site in range(N):
+                il = lp.get(site)
+                ir = rp.get(site)
+                if il is None and ir is None:
+                    transfer = E
+                elif il is not None and ir is not None:
+                    if lw[il] != rw[ir]:
+                        compatible = False
+                        break
+                    transfer = np.kron(left.c if il == 0 else I2,
+                                       right.c if ir == 0 else I2)
+                elif il is not None:
+                    transfer = np.kron(left.c if il == 0 else I2, A[lw[il]])
+                else:
+                    transfer = np.kron(A[rw[ir]], right.c if ir == 0 else I2)
+                product = product @ transfer
+            if compatible:
+                total += int(lc * rc * np.trace(product))
+    return total
+
+
+def exact_affine_solution(matrix, rhs):
+    reduced, pivots = DomainMatrix.from_Matrix(matrix.row_join(rhs)).to_field().rref()
+    if matrix.cols in pivots:
+        raise AssertionError("Gram normal equations inconsistent")
+    r = reduced.to_Matrix()
+    x = sp.zeros(matrix.cols, 1)
+    for row, col in enumerate(pivots):
+        x[col] = r[row, matrix.cols]
+    assert matrix * x == rhs
+    free = [j for j in range(matrix.cols) if j not in pivots]
+    null = sp.zeros(matrix.cols, len(free))
+    for k, j in enumerate(free):
+        null[j, k] = 1
+        for row, col in enumerate(pivots):
+            null[col, k] = -r[row, j]
+    assert matrix * null == sp.zeros(matrix.rows, len(free))
+    return x, null, len(pivots)
+
+
+def exact_solution(matrix, rhs):
+    x, null, rank = exact_affine_solution(matrix, rhs)
+    assert null.cols == 0 and rank == matrix.cols
+    return x
+
+
+def main():
+    base = local_basis(0)
+    kernels = []
+    for distance in range(3):
+        other = local_basis(distance)
+        block = np.array([[overlap(left, right) for right in other]
+                          for left in base], dtype=object)
+        kernels.append(block)
+    assert np.array_equal(kernels[0], kernels[0].T)
+    # A bond's left/right placements overlap; use independent columns from
+    # the exact same-bond Gram block before assigning a physical dual norm.
+    _, pivots = DomainMatrix.from_Matrix(sp.Matrix(kernels[0].tolist())).to_field().rref()
+    pivots = list(pivots)
+    assert len(pivots) == 20
+    local_dim = len(pivots)
+    blocks = [k[np.ix_(pivots, pivots)] for k in kernels]
+    for distance in range(3, N - 2):
+        assert overlap(base[0], local_basis(distance)[0]) == 0
+
+    dim = N * local_dim
+    k = np.zeros((dim, dim), dtype=object)
+    for j in range(N):
+        sl = slice(j * local_dim, (j + 1) * local_dim)
+        k[sl, sl] = blocks[0]
+        for distance in (1, 2):
+            l = (j + distance) % N
+            sr = slice(l * local_dim, (l + 1) * local_dim)
+            k[sl, sr] = blocks[distance]
+            k[sr, sl] = blocks[distance].T
+    assert np.array_equal(k, k.T)
+
+    g = np.zeros(dim, dtype=object)
+    for bond in (0, N - 1):
+        local = local_basis(bond)
+        for a, raw_col in enumerate(pivots):
+            g[bond * local_dim + a] = overlap(local[raw_col], source())
+    h = overlap(source(), source())
+    z = int(np.trace(np.linalg.matrix_power(E, N)))
+    assert h * 3 == 36 * z * 2
+
+    ks = sp.Matrix(k.tolist())
+    gs = sp.Matrix(g.tolist())
+    c0, null, gram_rank = exact_affine_solution(ks, gs)
+    residual = sp.Integer(h) - gs.dot(c0)
+    assert residual == 0
+
+    # Minimize the *physical* sum of squared bond vectors over all affine
+    # solutions. M is block diagonal because the primal row is each physical
+    # bond; the left/right local placements were already merged in K00.
+    m0 = sp.Matrix(blocks[0].tolist())
+    metric = sp.diag(*([m0] * N))
+    rref_numerator = (c0.T * metric * c0)[0]
+    correction = exact_solution(null.T * metric * null,
+                                -null.T * metric * c0)
+    c = c0 + null * correction
+    assert ks * c == gs
+    assert null.T * metric * c == sp.zeros(null.cols, 1)
+    numerator = (c.T * metric * c)[0]
+    assert numerator <= rref_numerator
+    upper = numerator / (36 * z)
+    rref_upper = rref_numerator / (36 * z)
+
+    output = {
+        "n": N,
+        "full_hilbert_dimension_not_built": 3**N,
+        "transfer_dimension": 4,
+        "raw_local_columns_per_bond": 24,
+        "independent_local_columns_per_bond": local_dim,
+        "global_gram_dimension": dim,
+        "gram_nonzero_bond_distances": [0, 1, 2],
+        "gram_rank": gram_rank,
+        "nullity": null.cols,
+        "ground_norm_integer_gauge": z,
+        "source_norm_normalized": str(sp.Rational(h, 36*z)),
+        "membership_residual_exact": str(residual),
+        "source_in_span": True,
+        "feasible_dual_upper_rref_exact": str(rref_upper),
+        "feasible_dual_upper_rref_decimal": str(sp.N(rref_upper, 12)),
+        "optimal_dual_upper_exact": str(upper),
+        "optimal_dual_upper_decimal": str(sp.N(upper, 12)),
+        "note": "The dual norm is minimized over the stated finite R3 local span with the correct per-physical-bond metric. All Gram data came from local 4x4 transfer contractions.",
+    }
+    path = Path(__file__).with_name(f'aklt_compact_gram_n{N}.json')
+    path.write_text(json.dumps(output, indent=2)+'\n')
+    print(json.dumps(output, indent=2))
+
+
+if __name__ == '__main__':
+    main()

+3. The operation developed here: exact compact local-row completion
+
+Input contract: a one-dimensional chain/ring of N sites; fixed local dimension d;
+finite-range rational matrices L_j; a nonzero rational MPS psi of bond dimension
+D; exact frustration-free constraints L_j psi=0; a fixed-support rational V;
+and a finite dictionary O_(j,a) on an interval of width at most R containing the
+support of h_j=L_j^*L_j. All matrices/tensors and rational bit lengths are input.
+There are at most s dictionary columns per physical row, with s fixed when d,D,R
+are fixed. Verify Z>0 and every ||L_j psi||^2=0 by exact contractions; the promise
+need not be trusted. Check V=V^* for the energy-curvature interpretation. This
+does not verify uniqueness of the ground state, which is
+unneeded for the algebraic bound after exact dual feasibility but needed for the
+simple physical nondegenerate energy-derivative interpretation above.
+
+Write w_j=sum_a c_(j,a) L_j O_(j,a)psi and a_(j,a)=h_j O_(j,a)psi.
+Let A be the column map with these a columns. Compute only
+
+    K=A^*A,  g=A^*b,  h=<b,b>,
+    M_(j,a),(k,b)=delta_(j,k)<L_j O_(j,a)psi,L_j O_(j,b)psi>.
+
+Each entry is an exact MPS transfer contraction. Solve Kc0=g, retain a basis T
+for ker K, and compute rho=h-g^*c0. Normal equations imply
+
+    rho=||b-Ac0||^2.                                    (2)
+
+If rho is not exactly zero, the specified dictionary returns UNKNOWN.
+This is a decision-relevant refusal, not a proof that no other dictionary works.
+If rho=0, all feasible coefficient vectors are c=c0+Tz. Minimize c^*Mc by
+
+    (T^*MT)z=-T^*Mc0.                                   (3)
+
+Within-row dependent columns may first be removed using their exact row Gram.
+Then M is positive definite and (3) has a unique solution for an independent T.
+Alternatively quotient its kernel. The resulting upper is c^*Mc/Z. Equations
+(2), (3), the tensors and rational coefficients form an exactly checkable witness.
+
+M is NOT K and is NOT the coefficient identity matrix. It includes all cross
+terms within each physical row. In particular two overlapping placements for a
+bond are merged before charging that bond's norm. Splitting one physical row into
+two independently charged copies changes the factorization and can spuriously
+reduce the norm. An initial root numerical probe made this mistake; corrected
+probes and every reported exact upper use the physical row metric.
+
+4. Why the Gram is local although the coefficients need not be
+
+If supp h_i is disjoint from supp O_(j,b), the latter support also contains h_j.
+Then h_i commutes with both h_j and O_(j,b), and
+
+    h_i h_j O_(j,b)psi=h_j O_(j,b)h_i psi=0.
+
+Consequently K_(i,a),(j,b)=<psi,O_(i,a)^*h_i h_j O_(j,b)psi>=0.
+This is an exact frustration-free identity. It is not exponential clustering and
+requires neither a spectral gap nor an inverse transfer matrix. Similarly g_(j,a)
+vanishes when supp h_j is disjoint from V, because h_j V psi=V h_j psi=0.
+M is block diagonal by the direct-sum definition of physical rows. In one
+dimension K is block banded, with a fixed cyclic bandwidth on a ring.
+
+The nonzero contractions insert operators on constant-width intervals. Prefix and
+suffix transfer products allow their environments to be obtained with O(N)
+arithmetic for fixed d,D,R,s (or a polynomial naive contraction routine suffices).
+No inverse transfer or spectral conditioning is presumed. There are O(N) nonzero
+blocks and O(Ns) coefficient variables. The implementation takes advantage of
+AKLT translation invariance, calculates three distinct blocks, and still loops
+over N transfer factors to calculate overlaps. Its exact dense coefficient solve
+is polynomial but is not claimed linear time. In general a banded singular Gram
+can have dense null vectors and a dense reduced system (3). Chain-wide completion
+is entirely compatible with fixed local block width.
+
+Bit costs: for rational input tensor/operator entries of at most B bits and fixed
+d,D,R,s, multiplying O(N) constant-dimensional transfer matrices produces entries
+of polynomial bit length in N and B. Denominators can be cleared by products of
+the input denominators; numerator growth is bounded by the logarithm of the
+number of fixed-dimensional contraction paths plus their entry sizes. The Gram
+dimension is O(N). Rank, nullspace and exact quadratic minimization can use
+fraction-free/rational elimination with polynomial bit complexity; determinant
+bounds make output coefficient bit lengths polynomial as well. Exact rational
+norm checks remain polynomial. This is a conditional algorithmic statement for
+fixed width/bond dimension and exact encoded inputs, NOT a uniform feasibility,
+useful-accuracy, floating-stability or practical-runtime theorem. Exponential
+dependence on increasing R or D, input acquisition and ground-state certification
+are all charged rather than hidden.

+# FM: scoped Frontier capability preservation
+
+N815 preserves a committed Ultra HIP investigation as negative and conditional research capital. Its source is Ultra commit `788beabca49c9821a86c8237b1328a53313a22c5`, a separate repository history. The original packet's own handoff states that canonical Astra Capital integration had not occurred. This intake copies exact decisive text, corrections, code/results and claim boundaries, and supplies a small selective archive of relevant worker reports. `package/hip_capability_v1/SOURCE_MANIFEST.json` names every copied member, byte hash, omitted class and the original full-packet manifest hash. Downloaded raw data and third-party PDFs are not duplicated here; the selected archive is not the full campaign.
+
+Read `frontier/dossiers/N815.txt` for the source-pinned pressure and isotope model results, exact failure scopes, and open review/acquisition gates. N702 addresses electrically shielded closed powder voids under a distinct polarizability interface. The HIP packet concerns connected pores in printed metal; it does not update or reuse N702's theorem. Existing rapid forging, isotope-coded HIP gas and curvature-selective deposition preempt broad novelty claims under the source's recorded primary-access scope. A registered gas assay and durable repair remain unperformed.
+
+`SOURCE_MANIFEST.json` and `DERIVED_MANIFEST.json` pin the FM selection and
+core synthesis. `SOURCE_COMPARISON.json` records exact byte comparison of all
+21 selected ZIP members, including 14 readable copies, against the separate
+Ultra commit. `SYNTHESIS.md`
+separates conditional mathematics, exact model
+obstructions, prior-art negatives and unperformed physical work.
+`python3 updates/FM/validate_hip.py` checks selected bytes/ZIP members,
+public source routes and append-only ledgers, card/gate wiring and the new-only
+checkpoint. `python3 frontier/build_access.py check --base-revision
+ace0cfc4437fe91c20ccd24d69e0ee4bb335e871` checks generated public access
+views for this branch snapshot. `VALIDATION.json` records passing local checks
+and their scientific limits. `PUBLICATION_STATUS.json` records the individually
+valid FM checkpoint plus the inherited global `unsupported checkpoint schema`
+failure. The integration remains an uncommitted isolated worktree draft;
+PR #83's pending N791–N814 entries require a fresh collision check and
+revalidation before remote publication. The FM branch can be proposed separately
+against main, with reconciliation required before merge if PR #83 lands first. Neither software check establishes mathematical correctness,
+historical priority or physical capability. New Frontier Genesis results require
+their own source-pinned intake rather than changing the HIP source packet.

+# FM HIP capability boundary
+
+14 October 2026. Capital base `ace0cfc4437fe91c20ccd24d69e0ee4bb335e871`.
+The selected source is the separate Ultra repository's committed HIP packet at
+`788beabca49c9821a86c8237b1328a53313a22c5`. That SHA is source provenance,
+not Capital ancestry. `package/hip_capability_v1/SOURCE_MANIFEST.json` identifies
+the original paths, exact hashes, readable Capital copies, selected worker-report
+archive and omitted classes. The full packet remains at the Ultra commit. Its own
+handoff recorded that Capital integration had not yet occurred.
+
+N815 preserves four different result types under one source-pinned scope, with
+separate proof ranges and two open gates. First, the ideal-gas cylindrical-throat
+model gives a conditional conservation law and pressure-slew exclusion. Its
+deficit bound includes the *initial* deficit: under the stated monotone-pressure,
+positive evolving-conductance and temperature/volume conditions,
+`Delta(t) <= max{Delta(0), sqrt(R_max/C_min)}`. Conductance, hot geometry and a
+gas-tight contact law have not been measured. Shrinking a throat to positive
+radius is not a seal.
+
+Second, an exact constructed pair keeps the whole room-temperature tracer map
+fixed while changing unmeasured hot creep. It reaches different declared hot
+geometric outcomes. It limits what a cold inverse query can decide under that
+information interface; it is not an observed alloy pair or a proof that every
+repair method fails.
+
+Third, a calibrated two-source isotope relation can identify the fraction of
+*retained* gas from the HIP source. Exact three-isotope ingress histories can
+share all endpoint counts and total gas while having different last-ingress
+times. Exchange can also erase a simple time inference. The proposed CT-registered
+single-pore extraction, calibration and actual hot uptake lower bound are
+unperformed. Endpoint isotope counts alone do not certify sealing time, net
+uptake or a durable bond.
+
+Fourth, the packet's recorded primary patent disclosures preempt a generic new
+rapid-forging operation and generic isotope-tagged HIP-gas/MS claim. Selective
+curvature deposition is known in other materials. None of these disclosures
+demonstrates the proposed alloy-compatible plug, single-pore assay or repair
+advantage. The source's 17,222 parsed pre-HIP morphology rows contain neither
+hot conductance nor paired process and durability labels. No qualified repair,
+novel physical operation, matched complete-resource advantage or
+civilization-enabling capability has been established.
+
+N702 is a conditional certificate for electrically shielded *closed powder
+voids* using a different metrology interface. It supplies no open-pore or
+printed-part bond/fatigue theorem. The FM card explicitly separates the scopes
+instead of merging them. The decisive next physical trial is a registered set
+of known sealed, open and throttled pores with blind source-resolved recovery,
+then matched HIP, rapid forging and verified full-preseal controls measured for
+bonding, regrowth, fatigue/leak and complete cost. Independent mathematical
+review remains open too. The new-only checkpoint records these obligations;
+the inherited global checkpoint validator still fails on unrelated historical
+schemas and is not reported as passing.

+ASTRA ULTRA — SCIENTIFIC CAPABILITY / v0001
+14 October 2026, Australia/Brisbane
+MISSION STATUS: NOT ACHIEVED
+
+No new scientific operation with a demonstrated consequential capability or
+complete-resource advantage was established. This campaign selected one real
+manufacturing task, constructed and tested three operations within it, and
+rejected generic novelty and unsupported sensing-to-action transfers. The
+strongest substantive output is a reproducible, corrected set of exact
+information/physical gates and a tightly specified hot-process assay experiment.
+That is research capital, not the requested breakthrough.
+
+The selected scientific task
+
+Repair fatigue-relevant defects in additively manufactured metal parts when a
+CT-visible pore may be sealed or connected to the surface through an unresolved
+throat. This matters for reliable complex metal components, including parts with
+internal channels where complete coating, machining and inspection are difficult.
+The desired capability is durable bonded repair at an improved complete cost or
+yield; a smaller CT pore alone is insufficient.
+
+Current primary evidence establishes the problem. du Plessis and Macdonald
+(2020, DOI 10.1016/j.addma.2020.101191) find connected/near-surface defects resist
+HIP or open as surface notches. Their specific reported sample outcomes do not
+come with a complete pressure-ramp trace. Tammas-Williams et al. (2016, DOI
+10.1007/s11661-016-3429-3) already document sub-XCT connections and surface-pore
+exceptions. Later pore tracing and reheating studies show that compressed pores
+can remain unbonded or regrow. These are established source findings, not ours.
+
+The action ambiguity is concrete: an apparently identical cavity can need only
+qualified HIP, or first need a gas-tight surface seal/encapsulation, a different
+process or rejection. External gas entering the open cavity removes the pressure
+difference needed for pressure-driven closure. The correct input is hot gas
+access plus evolving throat/contact/bond behavior, not room geometry alone.
+
+Selection and resources
+
+The bounded opening considered fast-charge lithium-plating control, electrolyzer
+degradation/action diagnosis, and metal-pore repair. Existing ultrasound/EIS/
+feedback methods narrowed the first two; the available datasets did not expose
+the proposed matched intervention outcomes. HIP had direct action-changing
+ambiguity, consequential manufacturing endpoints, actual controls and obtainable
+morphology data. It was selected before deriving the central mathematics.
+
+Six Sol Max and twenty-five Luna Max slots were assigned; one Luna failed
+without a readable contribution and receives no research credit. The initial
+independent scouts were then concentrated on this task, with one independent
+foundational/plasma operation investigation retained. Independence was instructed,
+not experimentally enforced; this allocation is not evidence that the research
+policy is superior. Root directly constructed the pressure-access certificate,
+normalized metrology, Kelvin redesign and isotope-source/clock queries.
+
+1. Rapid pressure before gas entry: constructed, then preempted
+
+Root investigated a pressure ramp that collapses or seals a connected throat
+before the gas equalizes. Under explicitly stated ideal-gas, common-temperature,
+cylindrical, continuum, no-slip assumptions,
+
+  n=pV/(RT),
+  n'=pi a^4(P^2-p^2)/(16 mu L R T),
+  q'=CP(1-q^2)+(c+theta-r)q,
+  C=pi a^4/(16 mu L V), q=p/P,
+  c=-V'/V, theta=T'/T, r=P'/P.
+
+Cavity compression and heating increase internal pressure and cannot be omitted.
+The near-equilibrium filling time is 8 mu L V/(pi a^4 P), with no extra RT.
+Unmeasured throat radius causes a fourth-power uncertainty. Sensitivity examples
+with illustrative geometry/properties are preserved; none predicts an actual

+# Direct hot-process gas provenance: construction and decisive limits
+
+The desired decision is whether to change printing/gas preparation, seal an accessible pore before HIP, or change the pressure/thermal process. Ordinary endpoint CT and total retained argon need not distinguish gas present before HIP from gas admitted during HIP. The proposed additional physical query is to use a calibrated stable-isotope argon composition during a small-coupon HIP trial, then extract gas from a CT-registered cavity under vacuum and measure total moles and isotope composition. It directly tests hot-process source rather than extrapolating a cold Xe/He transient.
+
+This is a **proposed diagnostic experiment**, not an acquired operation or a demonstrated repair. Generic isotope-tagged HIP gas, inert isotopes trapped in microporosities, and post-treatment mass-spectrometric readout are explicitly disclosed in EP3243585A1 (2016 priority; https://patents.google.com/patent/EP3243585A1/en, description around isotope-coded HIP and its argon table). Root inspected this primary patent. Its purpose is component authentication; it still preempts a generic new-operation claim. Individual fluid-inclusion noble-gas laser extraction/MS is established in minerals (Boehlke and Irwin 1992, DOI 10.1016/0016-7037(92)90126-4). Neither source establishes CT-registered single-micropore extraction and process control in an AM metal after HIP.
+
+## Exact consequence of the simplest source query
+
+Let f0 and fH be effective isotope fractions of retained pre-HIP and HIP-source argon, and let lambda be the fraction of retained gas originating in the HIP source. A calibrated two-source model gives f=(1-lambda)f0+lambda fH and lambda=(f-f0)/(fH-f0). This requires acquired endmember ranges that include fractionation, instrument mass bias, collection efficiency, initial-gas variation and any preferential loss. Bounds can be obtained by interval inversion; if the effective source ranges overlap or are unacquired, the implementation returns UNKNOWN.
+
+This identifies a **retained source fraction**. Isotopic counter-diffusion can replace original argon without adding net total gas. Therefore lambda is neither cumulative total ingress nor a seal time. Matrix/surface isotope uptake can also contaminate a pore extraction; blank subtraction and extraction localization are decisive physical calibrations. A positive source-specific isotope excess beyond all acquired blanks proves source atoms reached the sampled region; it does not alone prove a specific throat path or gas-tight bonding. A null signal requires an acquired sensitivity and open-path transport lower bound to rule out access.
+
+The synthetic interval test in isotope_query.py is reproducible, and an ordinary isotope-mixture decoder given identical measurements obtains exactly the same answer. There is no claimed algorithmic advantage. Any future contribution must be the physical query and its action-level validation or a material-specific resource advantage.
+
+## Why three argon isotopes do not give a general closure clock
+
+Even under favorable monotone no-outflow ingress, isotope counts are integrals y_i=integral f_i(t)dmu(t), with f36+f38+f40=1. They give total mass and at most two independent time functionals. For the physically admissible code f36=t/3, f38=t^2/3, f40=1-t/3-t^2/3 on [0,1], the positive measures
+
+    mu_A=(4/7) delta_(1/4)+(3/7) delta_(5/6)
+    mu_B=(1/6) delta_0+(2/3) delta_(1/2)+(1/6) delta_1
+
+have identical total mass, first moment 1/2, second moment 1/3 and all three isotope counts, but different last ingress times 5/6 and 1. Exact rational execution verifies this. No decoder can distinguish these model histories from those observations.
+
+An even simpler exchange adversary holds total moles constant. After a marker switch at t=1, let x'=k(t)(1-x). k=1 until cutoff 2 and k=1/2 until cutoff 3 give the same final x=1-exp(-1). The isotope endpoint reports integrated exchange, not the cutoff. Finite bins with three independent compositions can yield three bin masses only under a validated transport model and independently handled initial inventory. A small enrichment epsilon amplifies isotope count and blank errors by order 1/epsilon. No late-bin uptake bounds a seal time only if an open throat has a separately validated positive hot uptake rate under the challenge.
+
+## A physically bounded first test
+
+Use sparse engineered cavities on sacrificial coupons from one alloy/build, including independently known sealed, open, and throttled controls. Begin with a constant isotope composition for the whole cycle to avoid an unacquired fast gas-switching interface. Measure actual gas composition, pressure and temperature at the sample; quantify pre-existing argon, dead-volume carryover, surface/matrix uptake, extraction yield, vacuum blank, isotope discrimination and detector linearity. CT registration and blind sequential extraction must show that a single chosen cavity's gas can be separated from neighboring pores and the surrounding metal. Recovered isotope/mole balances must agree with known seeded standards before inferring source fractions in unknown defects.
+
+For scale only, an ideal 10 um-radius cavity at 100 MPa and 1200 K contains about 4.2e-11 mol total gas, or 4.2e-13 mol marker at 1% fraction. These are calculated quantities, not actual trapped inventories or detection guarantees. Published mineral/noble-gas instruments motivate feasibility; metal-specific backgrounds, laser release, aliquot split, dynamic range and recovery remain unacquired. Destruction means this is a process-policy experiment on witness coupons, not a same-part online controller. Transfer to production parts requires separate held-out validation.
+
+After calibration, compare printing, standard gas-HIP, rapid gas forging, and verified full-surface pre-seal/HIP arms on matched initial defects. Match heat treatment, surface finish and specimen geometry. Measure source-resolved gas, independently sectioned bonding, post-heat pore regrowth and fatigue or functional leakage. Give the existing-method comparator identical gas/CT/assay observations. Charge isotope procurement and recovery, dedicated lines, blank/purge cycles, sacrificial coupons, CT, extraction/MS, vessel work/thermal time, seal/removal, failed runs and functional testing. No quotes, facility access, full resource advantage or physical outcomes were acquired here.
+
+Decision: abandon generic isotope coding as a novelty claim and exact seal-clock reconstruction. A source-resolved pore assay is a narrower metrology hypothesis worth testing only with an existing small-coupon facility and validated extraction standards; it does not yet establish the requested new scientific capability.

+# Pressure access, sealing and useful repair are distinct operations
+
+Internal derivation, 14 October 2026. No alloy constitutive law was acquired.
+
+The selected task is durable repair of fatigue-relevant surface-connected pores in additive-manufactured metal, including pores whose narrow connecting path is unresolved by CT. The action is choosing a physically achievable repair process. The missing information is pressure-gas access and the evolving hot throat/bond state, not merely a reconstructed room-temperature pore shape.
+
+## Conservation before and after sealing
+
+Under ideal-gas, cylindrical, continuum, no-slip, quasi-steady, common-temperature assumptions, let external and internal absolute pressures be P and p, cavity volume V, throat radius a and length L, gas temperature T and viscosity mu. Write n=pV/(RT). Then
+
+    dn/dt = pi a^4 (P^2-p^2)/(16 mu L R T)
+    dp/dt = C(P^2-p^2) + p(T'/T - V'/V)
+    C = pi a^4/(16 mu L V).
+
+For q=p/P, c=-V'/V, theta=T'/T and r=P'/P,
+
+    q' = CP(1-q^2) + (c+theta-r)q.
+
+Shrinking the cavity and heating its gas increase internal pressure. Narrowing the throat decreases gas conductance. Neither effect can be dropped silently. These equations are conditional fluid mechanics, not a new physical law. Slip/Knudsen flow, nonideal gas, evolving complex throats, adsorption and gas dissolution require different or measured transport laws.
+
+After a genuinely gas-tight seal and with no dissolution/diffusion, n is fixed. At prescribed final temperature, p_f=p_s(V_s/V_f)(T_f/T_s). Without capillary or other closing traction, ongoing pressure-driven contraction to V_f requires
+
+    p_s/P_f <= (V_f/V_s)(T_s/T_f).
+
+If additional inward traction is bounded by Pi_max, replace P_f with P_f+Pi_max. This is a necessary quasistatic pressure-balance gate, not a universal volume floor in the presence of capillarity, plastic overshoot, gas loss or bonding. An adiabatic sealed gas has a different relation, pV^gamma=constant. CT disappearance alone does not establish a seal, diffusion bond, fatigue improvement or absence of regrowth.
+
+## A conservative pressure-slew exclusion certificate
+
+Suppose P>=0 is nondecreasing and absolutely continuous, P'<=R_max, p>=0, C(t)>=C_min>0, and c+theta>=0 on an acquired interval. Let Delta=P-p with Delta(0)<=D. At a putative first crossing Delta=D, necessarily P>=D and
+
+    Delta' = P' - C D(2P-D) - (c+theta)p
+           <= R_max - C_min D^2.
+
+Hence, by scalar comparison (or a strict barrier followed by a limit), if R_max<=C_min D^2, Delta(t)<=D throughout the interval. In general Delta<=max{Delta(0),sqrt(R_max/C_min)}. This excludes attaining a declared minimum pressure deficit if the coefficient bound remains valid. It does NOT rule out arbitrarily slow below-threshold creep or independent capillary/chemical sealing. If a throat law has no deformation below an independently measured threshold Y>D, it excludes pressure-induced throat sealing over that interval. If a finite-time creep upper bound is instead supplied, integrate that upper bound and compare with the required closure strain. A throat may reduce C as it closes; an initial C alone is insufficient for the certificate.
+
+The fourth-root critical-radius expression under constant geometry is
+
+    a_critical = [16 mu L V R_max/(pi D^2)]^(1/4).
+
+With fixed acquired geometry, a>=a_critical makes the slew bound at most D (provided the initial deficit is at most D). It is a sensitivity expression, not a numerical prediction for an alloy. The public sources do not provide the complete hot throat geometry, constitutive law and gas-property uncertainty needed to evaluate a physical certificate.
+
+## What a normalized contrast-gas query actually acquires
+
+For a fixed cavity, constant external step P_x, initial p=0 and fixed coefficient C_x,
+
+    p(t)/P_x = tanh(C_x P_x t).
+
+Suppose attenuation is y=b+s p/T_x. If the baseline y_0 and fully equilibrated y_inf are independently obtained without changing the cavity, normalized u=(y-y_0)/(y_inf-y_0) cancels b,s and gives p/P_x. An error bound epsilon on the ENTIRE normalized reading gives
+
+    atanh(max(0,u-epsilon))/(P_x t) <= C_x
+      <= atanh(min(1,u+epsilon))/(P_x t),
+
+with infinite upper endpoint when u+epsilon>=1. A missing response after finite time bounds transport; it does not prove isolation. Acquiring the equilibrium normalization of an almost isolated cavity may itself take prohibitively long. It must be replaced by an independently calibrated contrast/volume scale, with its errors charged. Mixtures of cavities, changing geometry and adsorption do not inherit the single-cavity formula.
+
+A hot coefficient interval requires an acquired transfer factor
+
+    C_H/C_x = (a_H/a_x)^4 (mu_x/mu_H) (L_x/L_H) (V_x/V_H)
+
+in this model, as well as the hot closure law. Without those inputs, the implementation returns UNKNOWN. Standard nonlinear fitting or c-optimal design given the identical observations has access to the identical coefficient interval; this is not an advantage over an equally informed method.
+
+## Exact action-changing ambiguity survives a perfect room tracer
+
+Two model worlds have identical geometry, gas laws and all room-temperature tracer observations. Give them different unmeasured hot throat creep coefficients m. In a restricted dimensionless hot model at P=1, fixed V, z=ln(a0/a),
+
+    p'=exp(-4z)(1-p),   z'=m(1-p),   geometric criterion at z=ln 2.
+
+Eliminating time gives p(z)=(1-exp(-4z))/(4m). For m=10, pressure at the criterion is 3/128. For m=1/10, the formal criterion pressure is 75/32>1; the trajectory stalls at z=-ln(3/5)/4<ln2. One world reaches the stipulated geometric criterion with a low gas inventory; the other cannot. A finite z means a POSITIVE cylindrical radius; a gas-tight seal needs an additional independently acquired contact, snap-through or bonding law at that event. The ODE alone does not supply a seal. The equality of the two complete room tracer maps is by construction, not a claim about an experimentally discovered alloy pair.
+
+The obstruction also survives full compressible Poiseuille flow. Let q'=tau^-1 exp(-4z)(1-q^2), z'=lambda(1-q), with q(0)=z(0)=0. Then
+
+    ln(1+q)=(1-exp(-4z))/(4 lambda tau).
+
+At z_s=0.1, lambda*tau=0.2 reaches the geometric criterion at q about 0.51; lambda*tau=0.01 approaches q=1 before that criterion. These worlds can share the same full room map. Literal sealing again needs the additional contact/bond law. Thus more accurate room imaging or room transient fitting cannot acquire the missing hot state-to-action link without a validated transfer or hot test.
+
+## Redesign tested within the same task
+
+Root proposed curvature-selective vapor condensation to close nanothroats at low pressure while leaving intended macrochannels open. The ideal wetting Kelvin relation is ln(p_v/p_sat)=-2 gamma V_m cos(theta_w)/(a R T), with geometry/contact-angle qualifications. This would directly change gas access, rather than infer it. But curvature-selective vapor deposition is already experimentally established (Lovikka et al., DOI 10.1039/C8MH01523F), and precursor fixation into a dense, alloy-compatible, gas-tight bridge that survives HIP is not supplied by that result. Low-melting volatile metals, oxides/polymers, byproducts, wetting and persistent interfacial films can destroy the required bonding or fatigue endpoint. No compatible HIP seal was acquired or demonstrated. The Kelvin calculation is a proposed physical gate, not a new established operation.

+"""Exact finite isotope-code ambiguity and conditional source-fraction assay.
+
+No actual isotope experiment. Standard mixing inversion is the matched decoder.
+"""
+from fractions import Fraction as F
+from itertools import product
+from pathlib import Path
+import json
+import math
+
+
+def moments(measure):
+    return [sum(w*t**k for t,w in measure) for k in range(3)]
+
+
+def source_fraction_interval(f_interval, native_interval, hip_interval,
+                             calibrated_effective_endmembers):
+    if not calibrated_effective_endmembers:
+        return {'verdict':'UNKNOWN: effective endmembers/fractionation/background not acquired'}
+    if hip_interval[0] <= native_interval[1]:
+        return {'verdict':'UNKNOWN: source intervals overlap'}
+    values = [(f-a)/(b-a) for f,a,b in product(f_interval,native_interval,hip_interval)]
+    lo,hi=max(0,min(values)),min(1,max(values))
+    if lo>hi:
+        return {'verdict':'REJECT_MODEL: no physical two-source mixture'}
+    return {'verdict':'CONDITIONAL_RETAINED_SOURCE_FRACTION', 'lower':lo,'upper':hi}
+
+
+def main():
+    # Two nonnegative ingress histories; first two time moments + total agree.
+    a=[(F(1,4),F(4,7)),(F(5,6),F(3,7))]
+    b=[(F(0),F(1,6)),(F(1,2),F(2,3)),(F(1),F(1,6))]
+    assert moments(a)==moments(b)==[F(1),F(1,2),F(1,3)]
+    # Physical isotope codes f36=t/3, f38=t^2/3, f40=1-f36-f38.
+    def counts(m):
+        return [sum(w*t/3 for t,w in m),sum(w*t*t/3 for t,w in m),
+                sum(w*(1-t/3-t*t/3) for t,w in m)]
+    assert counts(a)==counts(b)
+    # Constant-pressure bidirectional exchange: same cumulative exchange,
+    # distinct closure cutoffs. N is fixed; marker x=1-exp(-integral lambda).
+    exchange_a=1*(2-1)
+    exchange_b=.5*(3-1)
+    assert exchange_a==exchange_b
+    # Favorable source assay demo: endmembers here are synthetic calibrated
+    # values, not claimed natural abundance or actual purchased gas specs.
+    f0, fh = .0034, .01
+    true_fraction=.25
+    f=(1-true_fraction)*f0+true_fraction*fh
+    interval=source_fraction_interval((f-.00005,f+.00005),
+        (f0-.00001,f0+.00001),(fh-.00001,fh+.00001),True)
+    assert interval['lower']<=true_fraction<=interval['upper']
+    unknown=source_fraction_interval((f,f),(f0,f0),(fh,fh),False)
+    assert unknown['verdict'].startswith('UNKNOWN')
+    n=100e6*(4*math.pi*(10e-6)**3/3)/(8.314462618*1200)
+    result={
+        'scope':'exact model witnesses and synthetic calibrated source mixing; no HIP assay',
+        'moment_ambiguity':{'common_moments':[str(x) for x in moments(a)],
+            'common_isotope_counts':[str(x) for x in counts(a)],
+            'last_ingress_A':str(max(t for t,w in a)),
+            'last_ingress_B':str(max(t for t,w in b))},
+        'exchange_ambiguity':{'same_final_marker_fraction':1-math.exp(-1),
+            'cutoff_A':2,'cutoff_B':3,'net_molar_uptake':0},
+        'synthetic_source_assay':{'true_retained_HIP_source_fraction':true_fraction,
+            'conditional_interval':interval,'uncalibrated_verdict':unknown,
+            'strongest_same_data_decoder':'standard isotope mixture inversion; identical answer'},
+        'illustrative_ideal_gas_quantity':{'radius_m':10e-6,'P_Pa':100e6,
+            'T_K':1200,'total_moles':n,'marker_moles_at_1_percent':n*.01},
+        'novelty':'generic isotope-tagged HIP plus MS disclosed in EP3243585A1',
+        'physical_validation':False,
+    }
+    Path(__file__).with_name('isotope_query_results.json').write_text(json.dumps(result,indent=2)+'\n')
+    print(json.dumps({'passed':True,'scope':result['scope'],'interval':interval}))
+
+
+if __name__=='__main__':
+    main()

+"""Reproducible conditional HIP gates; no physical experiment or fitted alloy law.
+
+Python standard library only. All dimensional examples are sensitivity tests.
+Run from any directory; JSON is written beside this script.
+"""
+from fractions import Fraction
+from pathlib import Path
+import hashlib
+import json
+import math
+
+
+def pressure_coefficient(radius, length, volume, viscosity):
+    return math.pi * radius**4 / (16 * viscosity * length * volume)
+
+
+def step_pressure(p0, external, coefficient, duration):
+    """Exact fixed-geometry isothermal ideal-gas Poiseuille step, 0<=p0<P."""
+    assert external > 0 and 0 <= p0 < external
+    return external * math.tanh(coefficient * external * duration
+                                + math.atanh(p0 / external))
+
+
+def ramp_pressure(radius, length, volume, viscosity, rate, maximum, steps):
+    """Implicit Euler at endpoints of a linear ramp, with analytic root.
+
+    This convergent stepping is stable even for fast gas filling. Using the
+    endpoint pressure avoids a spurious half-step lag in the stiff limit.
+    Fixed throat and volume: it does NOT simulate sealing or material repair.
+    """
+    coefficient = pressure_coefficient(radius, length, volume, viscosity)
+    dt = maximum / rate / steps
+    p = 0.0
+    lag_max = 0.0
+    for j in range(steps):
+        external = rate * (j + 1) * dt
+        b = p + coefficient*dt*external**2
+        p = 2*b/(1+math.sqrt(1+4*coefficient*dt*b))
+        lag_max = max(lag_max, external-p)
+    return {"end_internal_Pa": p, "end_lag_Pa": maximum-p,
+            "max_sampled_lag_Pa": lag_max, "steps": steps}
+
+
+def tracer_coefficient_interval(u, error, external, duration):
+    """Normalized full-scale step response; error includes normalization error.
+
+    Fixed V,T; initial p=0; independently acquired full-scale response.
+    Does not infer a hot coefficient or certify sealing.
+    """
+    lo, hi = max(0, u-error), min(1, u+error)
+    return (math.atanh(lo)/(external*duration),
+            math.inf if hi == 1 else math.atanh(hi)/(external*duration))
+
+
+def hot_fill_verdict(coefficient_interval, multiplier_interval, pressure,
+                     duration, allowed_fraction):
+    """Only a fixed-geometry filling decision given an acquired hot transfer."""
+    if multiplier_interval is None:
+        return "UNKNOWN: hot transfer not acquired"
+    low = math.tanh(coefficient_interval[0]*multiplier_interval[0]*pressure*duration)
+    high = math.tanh(coefficient_interval[1]*multiplier_interval[1]*pressure*duration)
+    if high <= allowed_fraction:
+        return "LOW_FILL_CONDITIONAL"
+    if low > allowed_fraction:
+        return "HIGH_FILL_CONDITIONAL"
+    return "UNKNOWN: interval crosses decision"
+
+
+def main():
+    # Interior two-world witness. Same complete room pressure map, different
+    # unacquired hot creep. Locally linear hot flow model only. Finite z is a
+    # stipulated geometric/contact event, NOT a gas-tight seal from this ODE.
+    ell = math.log(2)
+    integral = Fraction(15, 64)  # (1-exp(-4 ell))/4
+    p_a = integral / 10
+    p_b_formal = integral / Fraction(1, 10)
+    assert p_a == Fraction(3, 128)
+    assert p_b_formal == Fraction(75, 32) > 1
+    z_b_limit = -math.log(0.6)/4
+    assert z_b_limit < ell
+    room_curve = [step_pressure(0, 1, .25, t) for t in [0, .1, 1, 10]]
+
+    # Full compressible model invariant: log(1+q)=(1-exp(-4z))/(4*m*tau).
+    z_seal = .1
+    numerator = 1-math.exp(-4*z_seal)
+    compressible = []
+    for mt in [.2, .01]:
+        exponent = numerator/(4*mt)
+        attainable = exponent < math.log(2)
+        compressible.append({"m_times_tau": mt, "criterion_attainable": attainable,
+            "q_at_criterion_if_formal": math.expm1(exponent),
+            "z_at_q_0_9": -math.log(1-4*mt*math.log(1.9))/4})
+    assert compressible[0]["criterion_attainable"]
+    assert not compressible[1]["criterion_attainable"]
+
+    # Sensitivity envelope, explicitly not source-measured HIP parameters.
+    volume = 4*math.pi*(10e-6)**3/3
+    length, viscosity, rate, maximum = 100e-6, 5e-5, 10e6, 100e6
+    rows = []
+    for radius_nm in [5, 10, 20, 50, 100, 500]:
+        radius = radius_nm*1e-9
+        coefficient = pressure_coefficient(radius, length, volume, viscosity)
+        r1 = ramp_pressure(radius, length, volume, viscosity, rate, maximum, 20000)
+        r2 = ramp_pressure(radius, length, volume, viscosity, rate, maximum, 40000)
+        # Slew barrier for constant C: Delta <= sqrt(Rmax/C), initial p=P=0.
+        barrier = math.sqrt(rate/coefficient)
+        assert r2["max_sampled_lag_Pa"] <= barrier + maximum/40000
+        rows.append({"radius_nm": radius_nm,
+                     "near_equilibrium_time_s": 1/(2*coefficient*maximum),
+                     "conservative_slew_barrier_Pa": barrier,
+                     "ramp_20000": r1, "ramp_40000": r2,
+                     "end_lag_discretization_difference_Pa": abs(r1["end_lag_Pa"]-r2["end_lag_Pa"]),
+                     "quasistatic_lag_approximation_Pa": rate/(2*coefficient*maximum)})
+
+    # Positive metrology in the supplied fixed-geometry model, followed by the
+    # indispensable UNKNOWN when hot transport has not been acquired.
+    true_c = .002
+    u = step_pressure(0, 2, true_c, 10)/2
+    interval = tracer_coefficient_interval(u, .001, 2, 10)
+    assert interval[0] <= true_c <= interval[1]
+    unknown = hot_fill_verdict(interval, None, 100, 1, .1)
+    assert unknown.startswith("UNKNOWN")
+    result = {
+        "scope": "internal exact algebra, fixed-geometry synthetic numerics and conditional acquisition gate only",
+        "physical_experiment": False, "novelty_established": False,
+        "linear_two_worlds": {"same_room_curve_both_worlds": room_curve,
+            "p_at_criterion_A_exact": str(p_a), "p_at_criterion_B_formal_exact": str(p_b_formal),
+            "world_B_closure_limit": z_b_limit, "criterion_z": ell,
+            "gas_tight_seal_law": "NOT ACQUIRED; finite radius is not a seal"},
+        "compressible_two_worlds": compressible,
+        "illustrative_parameters": {"pore_radius_m": 10e-6,
+            "throat_length_m": length, "viscosity_Pa_s": viscosity,
+            "ramp_Pa_per_s": rate, "maximum_Pa": maximum,
+            "alloy_creep_parameters": "NOT ACQUIRED"},
+        "sensitivity_rows": rows,
+        "tracer": {"measured_synthetic_u": u, "C_interval": interval,
+            "missing_hot_transfer_verdict": unknown,
+            "conditional_fill_at_transfer_1": hot_fill_verdict(interval, (1,1), 100, 1, .1)},
+        "trapped_gas": {"p_seal_Pa": 70e6, "P_final_Pa": 100e6,
+            "V_final_over_V_seal_min_isothermal_no_capillarity": .7},
+        "script_sha256": hashlib.sha256(Path(__file__).read_bytes()).hexdigest(),
+    }
+    out = Path(__file__).with_name("pressure_access_results.json")
+    out.write_text(json.dumps(result, indent=2, allow_nan=False)+"\n")
+    print(json.dumps({"passed": True, "output": str(out), "scope": result["scope"]}))
+
+
+if __name__ == "__main__":
+    main()

+#!/usr/bin/env python3
+"""Check the FM HIP source selection and public card wiring; no research replay."""
+
+from __future__ import annotations
+
+import hashlib
+import html
+import json
+import subprocess
+import sys
+import zipfile
+from pathlib import Path
+
+
+ROOT = Path(__file__).resolve().parents[2]
+sys.path.insert(0, str(ROOT))
+from state.publish_checkpoint import validate_record, views
+
+PACKET = Path("updates/FM/package/hip_capability_v1")
+CARD_ID = "N815-hot-pore-access-and-isotope-clock-acquisition-boundaries"
+ULTRA_COMMIT = "788beabca49c9821a86c8237b1328a53313a22c5"
+
+
+def digest(data: bytes) -> str:
+    return hashlib.sha256(data).hexdigest()
+
+
+def read_json(path: str | Path):
+    return json.loads((ROOT / path).read_text(encoding="utf-8"))
+
+
+def assert_recorded(path: str, expected: str) -> bytes:
+    target = (ROOT / path).resolve()
+    assert target.is_relative_to(ROOT), path
+    data = target.read_bytes()
+    assert digest(data) == expected, path
+    return data
+
+
+def main() -> None:
+    manifest = read_json(PACKET / "SOURCE_MANIFEST.json")
+    root_manifest = read_json("updates/FM/SOURCE_MANIFEST.json")
+    assert root_manifest["source_commit"] == ULTRA_COMMIT
+    assert root_manifest["selection_manifest"]["sha256"] == digest(
+        (ROOT / PACKET / "SOURCE_MANIFEST.json").read_bytes())
+    comparison = root_manifest["selected_commit_comparison"]
+    comparison_receipt = read_json(comparison["path"])
+    assert digest((ROOT / comparison["path"]).read_bytes()) == comparison["sha256"]
+    assert comparison_receipt["result"] == comparison["status"] == "PASS_EXACT_SELECTED_BYTES"
+    assert comparison_receipt["compared_count"] == comparison["compared_files"] == 21
+    assert comparison_receipt["copied_readable_count"] == 14
+    assert manifest["source_commit"] == ULTRA_COMMIT
+    assert manifest["source_packet_path"] == "research/2026-10-14-capability-v1"
+    archive = manifest["selective_archive"]
+    archive_data = assert_recorded(archive["path"], archive["sha256"])
+    assert len(archive_data) == archive["bytes"]
+
+    originals = set()
+    with zipfile.ZipFile(ROOT / archive["path"]) as zf:
+        names = set(zf.namelist())
+        assert len(names) == archive["members"]
+        for record in manifest["files"]:
+            rel = record["archive_member"]
+            assert rel not in originals and rel in names
+            assert not Path(rel).is_absolute() and ".." not in Path(rel).parts
+            originals.add(rel)
+            member_data = zf.read(rel)
+            assert digest(member_data) == record["sha256"], rel
+            assert len(member_data) == record["bytes"], rel
+            if record["capital_path"] is not None:
+                assert assert_recorded(record["capital_path"], record["sha256"]) == member_data
+        assert names == originals
+
+    full_manifest = next(
+        row for row in manifest["files"] if row["archive_member"] == "MANIFEST.json"
+    )
+    assert full_manifest["sha256"] == manifest["full_source_manifest_sha256"]
+    assert {row["path"] for row in root_manifest["selected_copied_files"]} == {
+        row["capital_path"] for row in manifest["files"] if row["capital_path"]}
+    for row in root_manifest["selected_copied_files"]:
+        assert_recorded(row["path"], row["sha256"])
+    for row in read_json("updates/FM/DERIVED_MANIFEST.json")["records"]:
+        assert len(assert_recorded(row["path"], row["sha256"])) == row["bytes"]
+    card_path = f"cards/{CARD_ID}.txt"
+    card_hash = digest((ROOT / card_path).read_bytes())
+    status = read_json(f"frontier/cards/{CARD_ID}.json")
+    assert status["card_sha256"] == card_hash
+    assert status["claim_status"] == "source_derived_unreviewed"
+    assert "No civilization-enabling capability is established" in (ROOT / card_path).read_text()
+    wrapped = (ROOT / f"frontier/review_cards/{CARD_ID}.txt").read_bytes()
+    assert wrapped.endswith((ROOT / card_path).read_bytes())
+
+    claims = [json.loads(line) for line in (ROOT / "indexes/claims.jsonl").read_text().splitlines()]
+    statuses = [json.loads(line) for line in (ROOT / "frontier/CURRENT_CLAIM_STATUS.jsonl").read_text().splitlines()]
+    assert len([item for item in claims if item["id"] == CARD_ID]) == 1
+    assert len([item for item in statuses if item["card_id"] == CARD_ID]) == 1
+    assert next(item for item in statuses if item["card_id"] == CARD_ID) == status
+    claim = next(item for item in claims if item["id"] == CARD_ID)
+    assert claim["status"] == status["claim_status"]
+    catalog = read_json("indexes/agent_catalog.json")
+    assert next(item for item in catalog["claims"] if item["id"] == CARD_ID)["card_sha256"] == card_hash
+    gates = [json.loads(line) for line in (ROOT / "frontier/OPEN_PROOF_GATES.jsonl").read_text().splitlines()]
+    own_gates = [item for item in gates if CARD_ID in item["card_ids"] and item["gate_id"].startswith("G-FM-")]
+    assert len(own_gates) == 2 and all(item["status"] == "open" and not item["completion_evidence"] for item in own_gates)
+
+    web_claims = read_json("web/catalog.json")
+    web_claim = next(item for item in web_claims if item["id"] == CARD_ID)
+    assert web_claim["text"] == (ROOT / card_path).read_text()
+    assert web_claim["source_ids"] == claim["source_ids"]
+    assert web_claim["source_paths"] == claim["source_paths"]
+    assert (ROOT / "web" / web_claim["url"]).is_file()
+
+    route = f"{CARD_ID}\t"
+    assert sum(line.startswith(route) for line in (ROOT / "agent/routes.tsv").read_text().splitlines()) == 1
+    topic_index = (ROOT / "agent/topics.txt").read_text()
+    for topic in status["topics"]:
+        path = f"agent/topics/{topic}.tsv"
+        lines = (ROOT / path).read_text().splitlines()
+        assert sum(line.startswith(route) for line in lines) == 1, path
+        assert f"{topic}: {path} ({len(lines)-1} cards)" in topic_index
+
+    refs = {ref["source_id"]: ref for ref in
+            status["proof_availability"]["located_proof_sources"] +
+            status["proof_availability"]["available_evidence_sources"]}
+    assert set(refs) == set(claim["source_ids"])
+    sources = {item["source_id"]: item for item in
+               (json.loads(line) for line in (ROOT / "indexes/source_metadata.jsonl").read_text().splitlines())
+               if item.get("source_id") in refs}
+    docs = {item["id"]: item for item in
+            (json.loads(line) for line in (ROOT / "web/documents.jsonl").read_text().splitlines())
+            if item.get("id") in refs}
+    assert set(sources) == set(docs) == set(refs)
+    for source_id, ref in refs.items():
+        source = sources[source_id]
+        doc = docs[source_id]
+        assert source["path"] == doc["path"] == ref["path"]
+        assert source["sha256"] == ref["sha256"]
+        page = (ROOT / "web" / doc["url"]).read_text()
+        assert html.escape((ROOT / ref["path"]).read_text()) in page
+
+    claim_map = read_json("updates/FM/CLAIMS.json")
+    assert claim_map["claims"][0]["id"] == CARD_ID
+    checkpoint_path = claim_map["claims"][0]["checkpoint"]
+    checkpoint = read_json(checkpoint_path)
+    validate_record(checkpoint, ROOT)
+    assert checkpoint["base_revision"] == claim_map["base_revision"]
+    assert checkpoint["parent_checkpoint_ids"] == []
+    branch = checkpoint["branch_id"]
+    projected = views(ROOT, {branch: {checkpoint["checkpoint_id"]: checkpoint}})
+    branch_path = f"state/branches/{branch}.txt"
+    assert (ROOT / branch_path).read_text() == projected[branch_path]
+    row = next(line for line in projected["state/branches.tsv"].splitlines()
+               if line.startswith(branch + "\t"))
+    assert (ROOT / "state/branches.tsv").read_text().splitlines().count(row) == 1
+
+    base = claim_map["base_revision"]
+    for path in ("indexes/claims.jsonl", "indexes/source_metadata.jsonl",
+                 "frontier/CURRENT_CLAIM_STATUS.jsonl", "frontier/OPEN_PROOF_GATES.jsonl",
+                 "agent/routes.tsv", "state/branches.tsv", "web/documents.jsonl"):
+        old = subprocess.check_output(["git", "-C", str(ROOT), "show", f"{base}:{path}"])
+        assert (ROOT / path).read_bytes().startswith(old), path
+
+    print(json.dumps({
+        "status": "PASS",
+        "scope": "selected committed source bytes, archive, N815 public wiring and new-only checkpoint; no scientific replay",
+        "source_commit": ULTRA_COMMIT,
+        "copied_files": sum(row["capital_path"] is not None for row in manifest["files"]),
+        "archive_members": len(originals),
+        "card": CARD_ID,
+        "new_open_gates": len(own_gates),
+        "scientific_correctness": "NOT_EVALUATED",
+        "novelty": "NOT_ESTABLISHED",
+        "physical_capability": "NOT_ESTABLISHED",
+    }, sort_keys=True))
+
+
+if __name__ == "__main__":
+    main()

+# FN: exact quantum-response construction and its capability boundary
+
+N816 preserves the committed Ultra Frontier Genesis packet as one scoped Capital card. Read `frontier/dossiers/N816.txt` with `root/PRINCIPAL_DERIVATION.txt`, `root/CORRECTIONS_v0001.txt`, `CLAIM_LEDGER.json` and `root/REPLAY_RECEIPTS.json` under `package/frontier_genesis_v1/source/`. The compact exact AKLT code/results, explicit-sector interval, right-placement obstruction and exact acquired-gap comparator are readable beside those files. `root/replay_selected.py` is copied so the selected finite replays can be executed in the original Ultra environment. Source scripts, results and worker reports are evidence for their exact internal scopes; no computation is rerun by this Capital intake.
+
+`SOURCE_MANIFEST.json` pins the actual separate Ultra source commit. The packet's original handoff has a precommit placeholder, preserved byte-for-byte. The selected deterministic ZIP and manifest name 54 archive members, including 28 readable copies. `SOURCE_COMPARISON.json` records byte comparison against `git show` of the frozen Ultra commit. The complete source packet remains in Ultra; raw data and PDFs are intentionally not duplicated in Capital.
+
+`SYNTHESIS.md` explains the conditional FF-MPS Gram operation, exact finite N6/N12 and older N20 evidence, narrow failed dictionaries, N764 prior scope, and the stronger same-information Knabe gap comparator. The mission remains `NOT_ACHIEVED / REDESIGN`; no all-N theorem, physical input acquisition, historical priority or matched complete-resource advantage is claimed. `validate_fn.py` checks source integrity, routes, card/gate status and its new-only checkpoint. `python3 frontier/build_access.py check --base-revision ace0cfc4437fe91c20ccd24d69e0ee4bb335e871` checks public access freshness. `PUBLICATION_STATUS.json` records the inherited global checkpoint schema error separately from the individually validated new checkpoint. This is an isolated worktree draft pending parent review and publication; the live PR #83 allocation N791–N814 must be rechecked for collision before push and reconciled before merge if it lands first.

+# FN Frontier Genesis quantum response intake
+
+14 October 2026. Astra Capital base `ace0cfc4437fe91c20ccd24d69e0ee4bb335e871`; separate Ultra source commit `e7ae999e957d70f98ccb9bd789c3eeb6c8229d30`. The source commit is provenance, not Capital ancestry. The source handoff JSON was written before that commit and contains a placeholder source pin. Its bytes are preserved unchanged; `SOURCE_MANIFEST.json` here records the actual commit and the selected files. The source full packet is 167 tracked files (about 67 MB). This intake preserves 28 readable critical text/code/result files and 26 additional selected worker reports/replay outputs in a deterministic archive. It does not duplicate raw scientific data, PDFs or unrelated source snapshots; omitted files remain at the separate Ultra commit.
+
+The strongest new scoped object is an **exact conditional computation** for supplied rational frustration-free one-dimensional MPS inputs. Fixed-width local dictionaries produce a block-banded transfer Gram by frustration freedom. Exact membership of the centered source in the column span is checked by `rho=h-g*c0=0`; if it fails, the operation returns `UNKNOWN`. If it holds, the physical per-row metric, including cross terms for overlapping placements on one physical row, minimizes a feasible dual norm and yields an exactly checkable upper response certificate. Fixed local dimension, MPS bond, operator width and dictionary size give a polynomial rational bit-cost construction in chain length and encoded input size. The coefficients may be global, and neither all-input feasibility nor useful accuracy is proved. Exact Hamiltonian/MPS input acquisition is outside the tested analytic AKLT fixture.
+
+For periodic AKLT spin-1, both three-site placements per bond are needed. Exact finite membership is reported at N=6–9, compact N=6/12 and an older N=20 RREF-only receipt. N=6 gives upper `159740147/109636215` and six-step Krylov lower `249983974783081804577822/172362641884453299405385`; an independently computed exact response lies between them. N=12 gives upper `627710130295322/439731204269175` without a lower. N=20 proves membership only in its source-version scope, with no optimized comparable norm and no 3^20 Hilbert vector. These observations do not prove all-N feasibility. Ultra root's selected exact copy-first replays cover N6 and N12; N20 is explicitly listed as not replayed.
+
+Three narrower negative lessons survive: a right-placement-only N6 dictionary has rank 71 and augmented rank 72, with nonzero left-null pairing; nearby-bond-only truncation fails even though each row operator is locally supported; and an initial numerical probe erroneously split overlapping placements into independent physical rows, spuriously reducing the norm. The corrected exact upper uses one physical row metric per bond. Tiny dual residual is also insufficient without coercivity because a low-energy component costs `delta^2/epsilon`. Exact feasibility handles the full kernel, whereas centering only one chosen state does not. Virtual-current and transfer identities are exact but no all-N parent-row peeling proof has been obtained.
+
+The current **matched comparison is negative**. Exact four-spin patch arithmetic plus the established Knabe finite-size mechanism acquires `H^2 >= H/10` for periodic N>=6 from the same local projector rows. The same six-step primal vector then yields upper `1.4537037411509957` and certified width `0.00336640557764377`, tighter than the local-row dual width `0.006664322136192456`. This is a rigorous finite interval comparison, not a complete wall-time/resource benchmark. Absence of a supplied gap cannot be charged as a competitor disadvantage when it can acquire one from the same rows. N764 already has feasible Hodge primal/dual intervals, full-domain TT overlap contractions and a winning sparse baseline on a different supplied interface. No generic duality or TT/MPS novelty, or Hodge-to-quantum bridge theorem, is asserted. Existing MPS response, local MPS/PEPS patch, complementary bounds, Knabe and locally gapped response methods constrain priority; focused nonidentity is not clearance.
+
+The campaign screened alternatives before selecting the testable quantum operation. Molecular H4/H6 PySCF input was obtained, but response-aware SCI overlapped LR-SCI/LR-SCI-PT and its held-out FCI comparison was privileged. Rare Schlögl paths gave too little barrier exposure and smFRET truth/interventions were unavailable. Physical atom writer, lithium and photonic routes lacked the acquired functional coupling, complete energy and decisive advantage interface. Euclidean stationary-varifold source reconstruction remained correctness-unknown with a smooth ambient curvature extension open. None is promoted to an additional card. Worker reports are historical and can predate root corrections; the root derivation, corrections, claim ledger and replay receipts govern current source status.
+
+The mission outcome is `NOT_ACHIEVED` and `REDESIGN`. A useful capability needs a nonintegrable exactly acquired/robust input, a proved low-cost source-specific completion and equal-information/equal-accuracy comparison with strongest response/gap/SDP methods at full acquisition, preparation, bit, tensor-width, verification and failure cost. A new all-N AKLT theorem alone would not establish that. No physical material experiment, historical priority clearance, externally reviewed proof or matched complete-resource advantage was obtained. The N816 card, scoped blockers, two open gates and new-only checkpoint preserve these distinctions. Capital copy/hash and access validators verify preservation and routing only.
