+
+Frustration-free annihilation makes the completion Gram block banded: sufficiently
+distant local defects have exactly zero overlap. It permits an O(N)-dimensional
+coefficient problem at fixed local width and MPS bond dimension. Rational
+contractions, exact rank tests and norm optimization have polynomial bit cost in
+N and encoded input length under those fixed-parameter assumptions. This is a
+conditional algorithm with UNKNOWN on failed membership; it is not a proof that
+fixed width always suffices or provides useful accuracy. The exact tensors are
+essential inputs, generated analytically here rather than measured from matter.
+
+What was actually established
+
+The test is the noncommuting periodic spin-1 AKLT Hamiltonian with analytic
+bond-dimension-two ground MPS and a one-site S_z source. Both three-site placements
+containing each bond are needed. Exact explicit-sector membership passes at
+N=6,7,8,9. Transfer-only exact completion passes at N=6,12,20. At N=20 the Gram is
+400 by400, rank317; the 3,486,784,401-dimensional Hilbert space is never constructed.
+That receipt comes from an earlier unoptimized RREF version and establishes
+membership, not an optimized norm or accuracy comparison.
+
+At N=6, independent explicit-sector and compact implementations return the same
+exact optimized upper 159740147/109636215. The exact six-step Krylov lower yields
+
+    1.450337335573352 <= chi <= 1.457001657709544.
+
+The interval is about0.4595% wide relative to its lower endpoint. An independent
+exact direct response reference is 287145511231/197956185875, approximately
+1.450550837609686. It is used for validation, not supplied to certificate selection.
+At N=12, exact240-by240 Gram algebra returns the optimized-within-ansatz upper
+627710130295322/439731204269175, approximately1.42748598280. No N12 lower or matched
+full-resource advantage is claimed. Root copy-first replays independently rerun
+the exact N6 interval, compact N6/N12 calculations, narrow obstruction, virtual
+identity and comparator; their precise receipts are in root/REPLAY_RECEIPTS.json.
+
+The decisive competitor
+
+An absent supplied gap is not a capability advantage when the same local
+projectors let a competitor acquire one cheaply. Exact rational LDL checks on an
+open four-spin patch prove B^2 >=(2/5)B. The established Knabe finite-size argument
+then proves H^2 >=(1/10)H for these periodic chains N>=6. The same six-step primal
+with this acquired gap gives the certified upper1.4537037411509957. Its interval
+width0.00336640557764 is smaller than our dual width0.00666432213619.
+
+This sufficient matched competitor defeats the claimed advantage on the tested
+instance. It uses the same Hamiltonian, source and primal, and includes actual
+gap acquisition instead of assuming an oracle. Stronger known gap methods may
+improve it further. The calculation is a comparison of rigorous widths; it is not
+a completed MPS wall-time/memory benchmark. The program does not claim to have
+implemented every best response solver. Exact finite-sector response is itself an
+additional strong comparator at these small sizes.
+
+Failures and corrections that must survive
+
+The right-placement-only ansatz fails exactly at N6 (rank71 vs augmented72), with a
+saved integer left-null witness dotting b to-3552. That does not refute the merged
+two-placement ansatz. Nearby-bond subsets fail; successful local-width rows still
+spread across the chain. An initial root probe incorrectly charged overlapping
+placements as separate physical rows and produced a spuriously halved norm; the
+probe was corrected before any reported exact certificate. Within-bond cross terms
+are now included in the metric. Old audit reports precede the transfer-only
+implementation; root/PRINCIPAL_DERIVATION.txt and CLAIM_LEDGER.json record the later
+evidence rather than silently editing those source reports.
+
+Centering b against one ground state does not ensure orthogonality to every
+ground vector. Exact dual feasibility establishes the necessary range condition;
+approximate feasibility does not. A small omitted component at energy epsilon
+can cost residual_squared/epsilon. A two-spin open-AKLT kernel counterexample and
+a pinned exclusion-chain example preserve those limitations. All-N AKLT
+feasibility, robustness to uncertain inputs and a useful source-specific
+advantage remain open. The virtual-current commutator and transfer eigenvalue
+-1/3 are exact but do not supply the missing parent-row peeling identity.
+
+Selection and alternative work
+
+Six Sol Max and25 Luna Max workers were used in this campaign: five complementary
+Sol leads each delegated four bounded independent screens, followed by one Sol
+and five Luna workers concentrated on quantum dual construction, proof,
+counterexamples, implementation, priority and synthesis. Counts describe
+allocation, not aggregate inference time or scientific evidence. The principal
+agent developed the central operation/representation, corrected the physical row
+metric, and acquired and proved the defeating finite-patch comparator.
+
+Molecular response had a fresh PySCF executable interface: H4 and asymmetric H6
+integrals, exact references and finite-field/selected-CI comparisons were actually
+generated. Response-aware SCI collides with existing LR-SCI/LR-SCI-PT and
+property-oriented selection. The strongest privileged result consumed the held-out
+FCI answer; it is not a usable algorithm. Rare-event acquisition used original
+Schlogl jump paths instead of supplying a rare transition matrix. Insufficient
+barrier exposure left the required rate unconstrained; prepared controls and real
+smFRET traces did not establish the missing decision/outcome. Weighted-ensemble,
+forward-flux and importance-sampling competitors remain substantial.
+
+Current experimental matter/energy/control papers were examined, including
+atomically buried CrSBr writing, NV readout, lithium extraction and a photonic
+nonlinear primitive. Existing physical successes do not supply the proposed
+functional coupling, complete device energy balance or a new computational
+advantage. Their exact unresolved interfaces are retained in worker reports.
+The independent foundational line recovered a pinned Euclidean stationary
+varifold manuscript from GitHub and exposed the curvature correction needed for
+a smooth-ambient extension. Availability and compilation are not correctness;
+the extension remains open and was not substituted for the failed main objective.
+
+Astra Capital was retrieved at ace0cfc4437fe91c20ccd24d69e0ee4bb335e871, with the
+unmerged draftPR83 allocations checked separately. N764 is close supplied-Hodge
+primal/dual capital; its acquisition boundary and sparse comparator remain
+relevant, but no theorem transfer is assumed. N768/N770, N752/N753 and N788/N790
+were screened with their precise interfaces. The three Pro directions were
+treated as complementary resources; thread read availability/status is recorded
+separately, and no unavailable or unreviewed Pro result is used as a premise.
+
+Priority, reach and investment
+
+The construction does not establish a new abstract duality. Complementary
+variational bounds, MPS Hylleraas and analytic/correction-vector response, local
+MPS/PEPS patch bounds, and finite-size gap criteria are prior art. Recent locally
+gapped response theory also blocks a generic “no global gap” novelty claim. The
+focused search did not locate an identical compact local-row upper, but priority
+remains UNKNOWN. Source-level comparison details and primary links are retained.
+
+The plausible technological reach is rigorous response computation for selected
+quantum materials/models if exact or robustly certified inputs, useful completion
+and matched advantage can be acquired. This campaign establishes none of that
+application reach, no physical control and no TypeI/II enabling operation.
+
+REDESIGN before major investment. Require a scientifically meaningful,
+nonintegrable source/input family where existing coercivity, response and SDP
+methods genuinely struggle; prove/implement the low-cost completion; then compare
+at matched accuracy, input acquisition, preparation, tensor width, bit cost,
+verification and failure rate. An irrelevant decoupled tiny-gap spectator is not
+evidence of advantage. An all-N AKLT theorem alone would deepen mathematics but
+would not rescue the defeated capability claim. Preserve the finite result and
+all failures rather than replacing the objective with an easier exact fixture.
+
+Versioning and publication
+
+The source packet is versioned in the Ultra repository. The installed molecular
+.venv, regenerated LaTeX builds and nested Git metadata are excluded; exact tracked
+public repository bytes are preserved in a plain pinned source snapshot. Source inputs,
+scripts, reports, raw accessed data/PDFs, dependency requirements and file hashes
+are retained according to SOURCE_MANIFEST.json. Package integrity/replay does not
+establish external review or novelty. Capital intake and actual Git publication
+are tracked separately in a publication receipt; this source report does not
+assert that a commit, shared PR or merge has already occurred.

+Let H=L^*L=sum_j L_j^*L_j on a finite-dimensional complex Hilbert space.
+Assume b is in Ran H. For any x and any row vectors w_j satisfying
+
+    sum_j L_j^* w_j = b,
+

+
+    lower(x) = (2 Re<b,x>-<x,Hx>)/Z,
+    upper(w) = sum_j ||w_j||^2/Z.

+Then lower <= chi <= upper, and

+    upper-lower = sum_j ||w_j-L_j x||^2/Z.                 (1)

+"""Independent root probe of an exactly feasible local quantum-response dual.
+
+Explicit AKLT MPS supplies ground state; dense arrays are validation only.
+Core Thomson/Hylleraas duality is established mathematics, not a novelty claim.
+"""
+from pathlib import Path
+import itertools
+import json
+import math
+import time
+import numpy as np
+
+def ground_mps(n):
+    a=[np.array([[0,math.sqrt(2/3)],[0,0]],complex),
+       np.diag([-1/math.sqrt(3),1/math.sqrt(3)]).astype(complex),
+       np.array([[0,0],[-math.sqrt(2/3),0]],complex)]
+    psi=np.array([np.trace(np.linalg.multi_dot([a[s] for s in word]))
+                  for word in itertools.product(range(3),repeat=n)])
+    return psi/np.linalg.norm(psi)
+
+sz=np.diag([1,0,-1]).astype(complex)
+sp=math.sqrt(2)*np.array([[0,1,0],[0,0,1],[0,0,0]],complex)
+sm=sp.T.conj()
+dot=np.kron(sz,sz)+(np.kron(sp,sm)+np.kron(sm,sp))/2
+p2=(dot@dot+3*dot+2*np.eye(9))/6
+assert np.linalg.norm(p2@p2-p2)<1e-13
+
+def local(op,sites,vec,n):
+    other=[j for j in range(n) if j not in sites]
+    perm=list(sites)+other
+    arr=np.asarray(vec).reshape([3]*n).transpose(perm).reshape(3**len(sites),-1)
+    out=(op@arr).reshape([3]*n).transpose(np.argsort(perm))
+    return out.reshape(-1)
+
+def local_dual_columns(psi,n,bond,r,offset=0):
+    # Contiguous periodic block starts at first site of bond. Outside Schmidt
+    # support is exactly the MPS-conditioned environment in this finite probe.
+    sites=[(bond-offset+j)%n for j in range(r)]
+    other=[j for j in range(n) if j not in sites]
+    perm=sites+other
+    arr=psi.reshape([3]*n).transpose(perm).reshape(3**r,-1)
+    _,s,vh=np.linalg.svd(arr,full_matrices=False)
+    keep=s>1e-11
+    env=vh[keep].T
+    inside=np.kron(np.eye(3**offset),np.kron(p2,np.eye(3**(r-offset-2))))
+    evals,evecs=np.linalg.eigh(inside)
+    columns=[]
+    for u in evecs[:,evals>.5].T:
+        for v in env.T:
+            columns.append(np.outer(u,v).reshape([3]*n).transpose(np.argsort(perm)).reshape(-1))
+    w=np.stack(columns,axis=1)
+    assert np.linalg.norm(w.conj().T@w-np.eye(w.shape[1]))<1e-10
+    return w
+
+def run(n):
+    t0=time.monotonic()
+    psi=ground_mps(n)
+    d=len(psi)
+    def act(x):
+        return sum(local(p2,[j,(j+1)%n],x,n) for j in range(n))
+    assert np.linalg.norm(act(psi))<1e-12
+    b=local(sz,[0],psi,n)
+    b-=psi*np.vdot(psi,b)
+    # Dense references up to N6; beyond that use a separately labeled implicit
+    # correction-vector CG reference, without claiming a certified error bound.
+    if n<=6:
+        h=np.column_stack([act(np.eye(d)[:,j]) for j in range(d)])
+        ev,u=np.linalg.eigh(h)
+        keep=ev>1e-10
+        exact=float(np.sum(np.abs(u[:,keep].conj().T@b)**2/ev[keep]).real)
+        reference={'method':'dense eigensolve','matvecs_for_dense_matrix':d}
+    else:
+        x=np.zeros_like(b)
+        residual=b.copy(); direction=residual.copy()
+        rr=float(np.vdot(residual,residual).real)
+        for iteration in range(1,1001):
+            hd=act(direction)+psi*np.vdot(psi,direction)
+            alpha=rr/float(np.vdot(direction,hd).real)
+            x+=alpha*direction; residual-=alpha*hd
+            new=float(np.vdot(residual,residual).real)
+            if new<1e-24: break
+            direction=residual+(new/rr)*direction; rr=new
+        exact=float(np.vdot(b,x).real)
+        reference={'method':'implicit correction-vector CG numerical reference',
+                   'matvecs':iteration,'residual':math.sqrt(new),'certified_error_bound':False}
+    rows=[]
+    for r,all_offsets in [(2,False),(3,False),(3,True)]:
+        groups=[]
+        for j in range(n):
+            w=np.concatenate([local_dual_columns(psi,n,j,r,offset)
+                              for offset in range(r-1 if all_offsets else 1)],axis=1)
+            if all_offsets:
+                # Two placements contribute to the SAME physical row w_j.
+                # Orthonormalizing the union charges its actual Hilbert norm.
+                uu,ss,_=np.linalg.svd(w,full_matrices=False)
+                w=uu[:,ss>1e-11]
+            groups.append(w)
+        a=np.concatenate(groups,axis=1)
+        c,_,rank,_=np.linalg.lstsq(a,b,rcond=1e-11)
+        residual=float(np.linalg.norm(a@c-b))
+        dual=float(np.vdot(c,c).real)
+        rows.append({'block_size':r,'all_contiguous_block_placements':all_offsets,
+            'columns':a.shape[1],'rank':int(rank),
+            'feasibility_residual':residual,'dual_norm':dual,
+            'numerically_feasible_only':residual<1e-10,
+            'upper_bound_claim':'NO exact/rational feasibility proof in this floating calculation; placement bases orthonormalized within each physical row',
+            'dual_over_exact':dual/exact})
+    return {'n':n,'hilbert_dimension':d,'ground_residual':float(np.linalg.norm(act(psi))),
+            'exact_response_reference':exact,'reference_status':reference,'dual_probes':rows,
+            'wall_seconds':time.monotonic()-t0}
+
+if __name__=='__main__':

+            'rows':[run(n) for n in [4,5,6,7,8]]}

+        for da,db in [(1,-1),(-1,1)]:

+
+def psd_pivots(matrix):
+    """Exact Schur/LDL certificate; zero pivot requires zero remaining row."""
+    a=matrix.copy(); pivots=[]

+            'nonnegative_ldl_pivots':[str(x) for x in pivots]})
+    return output
+

+

+COPIES = [
+    WORKER+'aklt_r3_obstruction.py', WORKER+'aklt_n6_interval.py',

+JOBS = [

+    (WORKER+'aklt_n6_interval.py', [], WORKER+'aklt_n6_certified_interval.json'),

+    ('workers/f_luna_dual_construction/aklt_virtual_current_identity.py', [], None),
+]
+
+def digest(path):
+    return hashlib.sha256(path.read_bytes()).hexdigest()
+
+def stable(value):
+    if isinstance(value, dict):
+        return {k:stable(v) for k,v in value.items() if k not in {'wall_seconds'}}
+    if isinstance(value, list):
+        return [stable(v) for v in value]

+
+def main():

+    output_dir.mkdir(exist_ok=True)

+"""Exact N=6 AKLT local-row dual and tangent-primal certificate.
+
+The source generator is the campaign's rational R=3 AKLT span probe. This
+script independently solves the row-norm-constrained completion, computes an
+exact full-sector response reference, and verifies a tangent-space lower
+bound. It is a finite exact diagnostic, not a scaling proof.
+"""
+from __future__ import annotations
+
+import json
+import runpy
+import sys
+from pathlib import Path
+
+import sympy as sp
+from sympy.polys.matrices import DomainMatrix
+
+
+HERE = Path(__file__).resolve().parent
+N = int(sys.argv[1]) if len(sys.argv) > 1 else 6
+SOURCE = HERE.parent / "f_sol_quantum_dual" / "aklt_r3_obstruction.py"
+sys.argv = [str(SOURCE), str(N)]
+src = runpy.run_path(str(SOURCE))
+
+zero_words = src["ZERO"]
+index = src["ZERO_INDEX"]
+psi_entries = src["PSI"]
+mag = src["MAG"]
+projector = src["Q"]
+columns_for_bond = src["columns_for_bond"]
+dim = len(zero_words)
+
+psi = sp.Matrix([psi_entries[word] for word in zero_words])
+source = sp.Matrix([mag[word[0]] * psi_entries[word] for word in zero_words])
+norm_psi_sq = (psi.T * psi)[0]
+assert (psi.T * source)[0] == 0
+
+# Exact parent Hamiltonian restricted to total S_z=0.
+hamiltonian = sp.zeros(dim, dim)
+for bond in range(N):
+    for col, word in enumerate(zero_words):
+        for in_pair, outputs in projector.items():
+            if (word[bond], word[(bond + 1) % N]) != in_pair:
+                continue
+            for out_pair, coeff in outputs.items():
+                updated = list(word)
+                updated[bond], updated[(bond + 1) % N] = out_pair
+                updated = tuple(updated)
+                if updated in index:
+                    hamiltonian[index[updated], col] += coeff
+
+# The full R=3 ansatz allows both placements of the spin-2 pair in each
+# three-site window. Reduce each row to an independent basis, retaining its
+# physical row Gram matrix so duplicate placements are charged correctly.
+row_bases: list[sp.Matrix] = []
+for bond in range(N):
+    row_columns = []
+    for placement in (0, -1):
+        row_columns.extend(columns_for_bond(bond, placement))
+    row_matrix = sp.Matrix.hstack(*row_columns)
+    row_bases.append(sp.Matrix.hstack(*row_matrix.columnspace()))
+
+dual_map = sp.Matrix.hstack(*row_bases)
+gram = sp.zeros(dual_map.cols, dual_map.cols)
+offset = 0
+row_dimensions = []
+for basis in row_bases:
+    count = basis.cols
+    gram[offset : offset + count, offset : offset + count] = basis.T * basis
+    row_dimensions.append(count)
+    offset += count
+assert gram.det() != 0
+
+# Minimum sum_j ||w_j||^2 over this restricted local-row ansatz.
+normal = dual_map * gram.inv() * dual_map.T
+lagrange = normal.gauss_jordan_solve(source)[0]
+coefficients = gram.inv() * dual_map.T * lagrange
+assert dual_map * coefficients == source
+dual_energy = sp.factor((coefficients.T * gram * coefficients)[0] / norm_psi_sq)
+
+# Exact response reference. The rank-one anchor removes the MPS ground vector;
+# centered source orthogonality makes this equal to H^+ source.
+anchored = hamiltonian + psi * psi.T
+response_vector = anchored.inv() * source
+chi = sp.factor((source.T * response_vector)[0] / norm_psi_sq)
+
+# Primal variational lower bound optimized in span{S^z_j psi}.
+tangent = sp.Matrix.hstack(*[
+    sp.Matrix([mag[word[j]] * psi_entries[word] for word in zero_words])
+    for j in range(N)
+])
+tangent_gram = tangent.T * hamiltonian * tangent
+tangent_rhs = tangent.T * source
+tangent_coefficients = tangent_gram.gauss_jordan_solve(tangent_rhs)[0]
+primal_vector = tangent * tangent_coefficients
+primal_lower = sp.factor(
+    (2 * (source.T * primal_vector)[0]
+     - (primal_vector.T * hamiltonian * primal_vector)[0]) / norm_psi_sq
+)
+
+assert primal_lower <= chi <= dual_energy
+result = {
+    "n": N,
+    "hilbert_dimension_total_sz_0": dim,
+    "mps_bond_dimension": 2,
+    "block_size": 3,
+    "placements_per_bond": ["left", "right"],
+    "independent_local_row_dimensions": row_dimensions,
+    "dual_map_rank": DomainMatrix.from_Matrix(dual_map).to_field().rank(),
+    "feasible_exactly": True,
+    "chi_exact": str(chi),
+    "primal_lower_exact": str(primal_lower),
+    "dual_upper_exact": str(dual_energy),
+    "lower_le_chi_le_upper_exact": True,
+    "upper_over_chi_exact": str(sp.factor(dual_energy / chi)),
+    "upper_over_chi": float(dual_energy / chi),
+    "interval_width_exact": str(sp.factor(dual_energy - primal_lower)),
+    "interval_width": float(dual_energy - primal_lower),
+    "scope": "finite exact AKLT diagnostic only; no all-N construction or scaling claim",
+}
+out = HERE / f"aklt_r3_exact_certificate_n{N}.json"
+out.write_text(json.dumps(result, indent=2) + "\n")
+print(json.dumps(result, indent=2))

+#!/usr/bin/env python3
+"""Compact exact Gram feasibility for local AKLT susceptibility duals.
+
+No 3**N vector or matrix is constructed. Each local column is a three-site
+rank-one operator acting on the integer-gauge AKLT MPS. Gram entries use 4x4
+transfer matrices and exact signed integers after scaling each column by 6.
+Only bond separations 0, 1, and 2 can contribute to the Gram matrix.
+"""
+
+from dataclasses import dataclass
+import json
+from pathlib import Path
+import sys
+
+import numpy as np
+import sympy as sp
+from sympy.polys.matrices import DomainMatrix
+
+
+N = int(sys.argv[1]) if len(sys.argv) > 1 else 6
+assert N >= 6
+A = (
+    np.array([[0, 2], [0, 0]], dtype=object),
+    np.array([[-1, 0], [0, 1]], dtype=object),
+    np.array([[0, 0], [-1, 0]], dtype=object),
+)
+I2 = np.eye(2, dtype=object)
+E = sum((np.kron(a, a) for a in A), np.zeros((4, 4), dtype=object))
+MAG = (1, 0, -1)
+PAIR_BASIS = ((0, 0), (0, 1), (0, 2), (1, 2), (2, 2))
+V_BASIS = ((0, 1, 1), (0, 1, 2), (1, 1, 1), (1, 1, 2))
+Q6 = {
+    (0, 0): {(0, 0): 6},
+    (0, 1): {(0, 1): 3, (1, 0): 3},
+    (0, 2): {(0, 2): 1, (1, 1): 2, (2, 0): 1},
+    (1, 2): {(1, 2): 3, (2, 1): 3},
+    (2, 2): {(2, 2): 6},
+}
+
+
+@dataclass(frozen=True)
+class Defect:
+    sites: tuple[int, ...]
+    q6: dict[tuple[int, ...], int]
+    c: np.ndarray
+
+
+def dual(bond, offset, u, v):
+    sites = tuple((bond + offset + t) % N for t in range(3))
+    pair_pos = -offset
+    q6 = {}
+    for pair, coeff in Q6[u[pair_pos:pair_pos + 2]].items():
+        word = list(u)
+        word[pair_pos:pair_pos + 2] = pair
+        q6[tuple(word)] = coeff
+    c = A[v[0]] @ A[v[1]] @ A[v[2]]
+    return Defect(sites, q6, c)
+
+
+def source():
+    return (
+        Defect((0,), {(0,): 6}, A[0]),
+        Defect((0,), {(2,): -6}, A[2]),
+    )
+
+
+def local_basis(bond):
+    out = []
+    for offset in (0, -1):
+        for v in V_BASIS:
+            mv = sum(MAG[t] for t in v)
+            for pair in PAIR_BASIS:
+                for spectator in range(3):
+                    u = (*pair, spectator) if offset == 0 else (spectator, *pair)
+                    if sum(MAG[t] for t in u) == mv:
+                        out.append(dual(bond, offset, u, v))
+    assert len(out) == 24
+    return out
+
+
+def overlap(left, right):
+    """Exact overlap of *six-times-scaled* states via 4x4 transfers."""
+    if isinstance(left, tuple):
+        return sum(overlap(item, right) for item in left)
+    if isinstance(right, tuple):
+        return sum(overlap(left, item) for item in right)
+    lp = {site: p for p, site in enumerate(left.sites)}
+    rp = {site: p for p, site in enumerate(right.sites)}
+    total = 0
+    for lw, lc in left.q6.items():
+        for rw, rc in right.q6.items():
+            product = np.eye(4, dtype=object)
+            compatible = True
+            for site in range(N):
+                il = lp.get(site)
+                ir = rp.get(site)
+                if il is None and ir is None:
+                    transfer = E
+                elif il is not None and ir is not None:
+                    if lw[il] != rw[ir]:
+                        compatible = False
+                        break
+                    transfer = np.kron(left.c if il == 0 else I2,
+                                       right.c if ir == 0 else I2)
+                elif il is not None:
+                    transfer = np.kron(left.c if il == 0 else I2, A[lw[il]])
+                else:
+                    transfer = np.kron(A[rw[ir]], right.c if ir == 0 else I2)
+                product = product @ transfer
+            if compatible:
+                total += int(lc * rc * np.trace(product))
+    return total
+
+
+def exact_affine_solution(matrix, rhs):
+    reduced, pivots = DomainMatrix.from_Matrix(matrix.row_join(rhs)).to_field().rref()
+    if matrix.cols in pivots:
+        raise AssertionError("Gram normal equations inconsistent")
+    r = reduced.to_Matrix()
+    x = sp.zeros(matrix.cols, 1)
+    for row, col in enumerate(pivots):
+        x[col] = r[row, matrix.cols]
+    assert matrix * x == rhs
+    free = [j for j in range(matrix.cols) if j not in pivots]
+    null = sp.zeros(matrix.cols, len(free))
+    for k, j in enumerate(free):
+        null[j, k] = 1
+        for row, col in enumerate(pivots):
+            null[col, k] = -r[row, j]
+    assert matrix * null == sp.zeros(matrix.rows, len(free))
+    return x, null, len(pivots)
+
+
+def exact_solution(matrix, rhs):
+    x, null, rank = exact_affine_solution(matrix, rhs)
+    assert null.cols == 0 and rank == matrix.cols
+    return x
+
+
+def main():
+    base = local_basis(0)
+    kernels = []
+    for distance in range(3):
+        other = local_basis(distance)
+        block = np.array([[overlap(left, right) for right in other]
+                          for left in base], dtype=object)
+        kernels.append(block)
+    assert np.array_equal(kernels[0], kernels[0].T)
+    # A bond's left/right placements overlap; use independent columns from
+    # the exact same-bond Gram block before assigning a physical dual norm.
+    _, pivots = DomainMatrix.from_Matrix(sp.Matrix(kernels[0].tolist())).to_field().rref()
+    pivots = list(pivots)
+    assert len(pivots) == 20
+    local_dim = len(pivots)
+    blocks = [k[np.ix_(pivots, pivots)] for k in kernels]
+    for distance in range(3, N - 2):
+        assert overlap(base[0], local_basis(distance)[0]) == 0
+
+    dim = N * local_dim
+    k = np.zeros((dim, dim), dtype=object)
+    for j in range(N):
+        sl = slice(j * local_dim, (j + 1) * local_dim)
+        k[sl, sl] = blocks[0]
+        for distance in (1, 2):
+            l = (j + distance) % N
+            sr = slice(l * local_dim, (l + 1) * local_dim)
+            k[sl, sr] = blocks[distance]
+            k[sr, sl] = blocks[distance].T
+    assert np.array_equal(k, k.T)
+
+    g = np.zeros(dim, dtype=object)
+    for bond in (0, N - 1):
+        local = local_basis(bond)
+        for a, raw_col in enumerate(pivots):

+    ks = sp.Matrix(k.tolist())
+    gs = sp.Matrix(g.tolist())
+    c0, null, gram_rank = exact_affine_solution(ks, gs)

+    # solutions. M is block diagonal because the primal row is each physical
+    # bond; the left/right local placements were already merged in K00.

+                                -null.T * metric * c0)

+    assert ks * c == gs
+    assert null.T * metric * c == sp.zeros(null.cols, 1)
+    numerator = (c.T * metric * c)[0]
+    assert numerator <= rref_numerator
+    upper = numerator / (36 * z)
+    rref_upper = rref_numerator / (36 * z)
+

+        "n": N,
+        "full_hilbert_dimension_not_built": 3**N,
+        "transfer_dimension": 4,
+        "raw_local_columns_per_bond": 24,
+        "independent_local_columns_per_bond": local_dim,

+#!/usr/bin/env python3
+"""Exact AKLT N=6 susceptibility interval from primal and local dual witnesses.
+
+The local dual uses the union of left and right three-site placements for each
+physical bond. Each bond's overlapping placement columns are merged into one
+subspace and its orthogonal projector before minimizing the dual norm.
+"""
+
+import json
+from pathlib import Path
+
+import sympy as sp
+from sympy.polys.matrices import DomainMatrix
+
+import aklt_r3_obstruction as ak
+
+assert ak.N == 6
+D = len(ak.ZERO)
+psi = sp.Matrix([ak.PSI[word] for word in ak.ZERO])
+norm = psi.dot(psi)
+b = ak.B
+
+
+def rational_solution(matrix: sp.Matrix, rhs: sp.Matrix) -> sp.Matrix:
+    aug = matrix.row_join(rhs)
+    reduced, pivots = DomainMatrix.from_Matrix(aug).to_field().rref()
+    assert matrix.cols not in pivots
+    r = reduced.to_Matrix()
+    out = sp.zeros(matrix.cols, 1)
+    for row, col in enumerate(pivots):
+        out[col] = r[row, matrix.cols]
+    assert matrix * out == rhs
+    return out
+
+
+def bond_projector(j: int) -> sp.Matrix:
+    k = (j + 1) % ak.N
+    p = sp.zeros(D)
+    for word, col in ak.ZERO_INDEX.items():
+        for pair, coeff in ak.Q[(word[j], word[k])].items():
+            changed = list(word)
+            changed[j], changed[k] = pair
+            p[ak.ZERO_INDEX[tuple(changed)], col] += coeff
+    assert p * p == p
+    return p
+
+
+def main() -> None:
+    bonds = [bond_projector(j) for j in range(ak.N)]
+    h = sum(bonds, sp.zeros(D))
+    assert h * psi == sp.zeros(D, 1)
+
+    local_projectors = []
+    local_ranks = []
+    for j in range(ak.N):
+        columns = [col for offset in (0, -1)
+                   for col in ak.columns_for_bond(j, offset)]
+        raw = sp.Matrix.hstack(*columns)
+        _, pivots = DomainMatrix.from_Matrix(raw).to_field().rref()
+        basis = raw[:, list(pivots)]
+        local_ranks.append(basis.cols)
+        projection = basis * (basis.T * basis).inv() * basis.T
+        assert projection * projection == projection
+        assert bonds[j] * projection == projection
+        local_projectors.append(projection)
+
+    q = sum(local_projectors, sp.zeros(D))
+    y = rational_solution(q, b)
+    w = [projection * y for projection in local_projectors]
+    assert sum(w, sp.zeros(D, 1)) == b
+    upper = sum(wj.dot(wj) for wj in w) / norm
+    assert upper == b.dot(y) / norm
+
+    # Six-step Galerkin/Krylov primal lower witness.
+    vectors = []
+    v = b
+    for _ in range(6):
+        vectors.append(v)
+        v = h * v
+    gram = sp.Matrix([[vi.dot(h * vj) for vj in vectors]
+                      for vi in vectors])
+    rhs = sp.Matrix([b.dot(vi) for vi in vectors])
+    coeff = gram.inv() * rhs
+    x = sum((coeff[i] * vectors[i] for i in range(len(vectors))),
+            sp.zeros(D, 1))
+    lower = (2 * b.dot(x) - x.dot(h * x)) / norm
+    assert lower == rhs.dot(coeff) / norm
+    primal_residual = b - h * x
+    residual_squared = primal_residual.dot(primal_residual) / norm
+    gap = sum((wj - bonds[j] * x).dot(wj - bonds[j] * x)
+              for j, wj in enumerate(w)) / norm
+    assert gap == upper - lower
+
+    out = {
+        "model": "periodic spin-1 AKLT, six sites, exact MPS ground state",
+        "source": "b=S_z(0)|psi>, with <psi|b>=0",
+        "physical_hilbert_dimension": 3**ak.N,
+        "sz_zero_dimension": D,
+        "local_block_size": 3,
+        "local_placements_per_bond": 2,
+        "local_dual_ranks_by_bond": local_ranks,
+        "source_in_exact_dual_span": True,
+        "primal_krylov_steps": len(vectors),
+        "lower_exact": str(lower),
+        "primal_residual_squared_exact": str(residual_squared),
+        "primal_residual_squared_decimal": str(sp.N(residual_squared, 16)),
+        "residual_gap_upper_if_gamma_at_least_one_tenth_exact": str(lower + 10 * residual_squared),
+        "residual_gap_upper_if_gamma_at_least_one_tenth_decimal": str(sp.N(lower + 10 * residual_squared, 16)),
+        "gap_lower_bound_needed_to_beat_local_dual_exact": str(residual_squared / (upper - lower)),
+        "upper_exact": str(upper),
+        "gap_exact": str(gap),
+        "lower_decimal": str(sp.N(lower, 16)),
+        "upper_decimal": str(sp.N(upper, 16)),
+        "relative_interval_width_over_lower": str(sp.N(gap / lower, 8)),
+        "exact_zero_checks": {
+            "H_ground": True,
+            "dual_sum_minus_b": True,
+            "duality_gap_identity": True,
+            "local_bond_projector_action": True,
+        },
+        "status": "finite exact certificate; no all-N theorem, physical acquisition, or comparative advantage",
+    }
+    path = Path(__file__).with_name('aklt_n6_certified_interval.json')
+    path.write_text(json.dumps(out, indent=2) + '\n')
+    print(json.dumps(out, indent=2))
+
+
+if __name__ == '__main__':
+    main()

+#!/usr/bin/env python3
+"""Rational six-site AKLT obstruction to a three-site local dual ansatz.
+
+The matrix columns equal the span obtained by applying the spin-2 projector
+on a pair inside each contiguous three-site block, tensored with the exact
+outside Schmidt support of the periodic AKLT ground state. Everything is
+restricted to total S_z=0, which contains the source S_z(0)|psi>.
+"""
+
+from itertools import product
+import sys
+
+import sympy as sp
+from sympy.polys.matrices import DomainMatrix
+
+
+N = int(sys.argv[1]) if len(sys.argv) > 1 else 6
+R = 3
+WORDS = list(product(range(3), repeat=N))
+MAG = (1, 0, -1)
+ZERO = [w for w in WORDS if sum(MAG[s] for s in w) == 0]
+ZERO_INDEX = {w: i for i, w in enumerate(ZERO)}
+INSIDE = list(product(range(3), repeat=R))
+OUTSIDE = list(product(range(3), repeat=N - R))
+OUTSIDE_INDEX = {w: i for i, w in enumerate(OUTSIDE)}
+
+# An integer-gauge AKLT MPS; periodic traces agree with the standard
+# A+=(sqrt(2/3)) sigma+, A0=-(1/sqrt(3)) sigmaz,
+# A-=-(sqrt(2/3)) sigma- up to one common factor per site.
+A = (
+    sp.Matrix([[0, 2], [0, 0]]),
+    sp.Matrix([[-1, 0], [0, 1]]),
+    sp.Matrix([[0, 0], [-1, 0]]),
+)
+
+
+def amp(word):
+    p = sp.eye(2)
+    for s in word:
+        p *= A[s]
+    return sp.trace(p)
+
+
+PSI = {w: amp(w) for w in ZERO}
+B = sp.Matrix([MAG[w[0]] * PSI[w] for w in ZERO])
+assert B != sp.zeros(len(ZERO), 1)
+assert sum(PSI[w] * B[ZERO_INDEX[w]] for w in ZERO) == 0
+
+# Projector onto pair total spin 2, all rational in the spin-z basis.
+Q = {
+    (0, 0): {(0, 0): sp.Integer(1)},
+    (0, 1): {(0, 1): sp.Rational(1, 2), (1, 0): sp.Rational(1, 2)},
+    (1, 0): {(0, 1): sp.Rational(1, 2), (1, 0): sp.Rational(1, 2)},
+    (0, 2): {(0, 2): sp.Rational(1, 6), (1, 1): sp.Rational(1, 3), (2, 0): sp.Rational(1, 6)},
+    (1, 1): {(0, 2): sp.Rational(1, 3), (1, 1): sp.Rational(2, 3), (2, 0): sp.Rational(1, 3)},
+    (2, 0): {(0, 2): sp.Rational(1, 6), (1, 1): sp.Rational(1, 3), (2, 0): sp.Rational(1, 6)},
+    (1, 2): {(1, 2): sp.Rational(1, 2), (2, 1): sp.Rational(1, 2)},
+    (2, 1): {(1, 2): sp.Rational(1, 2), (2, 1): sp.Rational(1, 2)},
+    (2, 2): {(2, 2): sp.Integer(1)},
+}
+
+
+def joined(block, outside, sites, other):
+    word = [0] * N
+    for j, s in zip(sites, block):
+        word[j] = s
+    for j, s in zip(other, outside):
+        word[j] = s
+    return tuple(word)
+
+
+def columns_for_bond(j, start_offset=0):
+    assert start_offset in (0, -1)
+    sites = [(j + start_offset + t) % N for t in range(R)]
+    other = [t for t in range(N) if t not in sites]
+    pair_pos = -start_offset
+    # Rows of the Schmidt reshaping span exactly the outside Schmidt support.
+    rows = []
+    for inside in INSIDE:
+        rows.append(sp.Matrix([[PSI.get(joined(inside, outside, sites, other), 0)
+                                for outside in OUTSIDE]]))
+    env_basis = sp.Matrix.vstack(*rows).rowspace()
+    assert len(env_basis) == 4
+    cols = []
+    for v in env_basis:
+        nonzero = [OUTSIDE[t] for t, value in enumerate(v) if value]
+        assert nonzero
+        outside_mag = sum(MAG[s] for s in nonzero[0])
+        assert all(sum(MAG[s] for s in w) == outside_mag for w in nonzero)
+        for inside in INSIDE:
+            if sum(MAG[s] for s in inside) != -outside_mag:
+                continue
+            col = sp.zeros(len(ZERO), 1)
+            for out_pair, coeff in Q[inside[pair_pos:pair_pos + 2]].items():
+                block_list = list(inside)
+                block_list[pair_pos:pair_pos + 2] = out_pair
+                block = tuple(block_list)
+                for outside in nonzero:
+                    word = joined(block, outside, sites, other)
+                    col[ZERO_INDEX[word]] += coeff * v[OUTSIDE_INDEX[outside]]
+            if col != sp.zeros(len(ZERO), 1):
+                cols.append(col)
+    return cols
+
+
+def main():
+    import json
+    from pathlib import Path
+
+    if N == 6:
+        cols = [col for j in range(N) for col in columns_for_bond(j)]
+        C = sp.Matrix.hstack(*cols)
+        # Exact rational left-null witness for the narrow right-only ansatz.
+        rank = DomainMatrix.from_Matrix(C).to_field().rank()
+        augmented_rank = DomainMatrix.from_Matrix(C.row_join(B)).to_field().rank()
+        assert augmented_rank == rank + 1
+        left_null = DomainMatrix.from_Matrix(C.T).to_field().nullspace().to_Matrix()
+        witness = next((left_null.row(i).T for i in range(left_null.rows)
+                        if left_null.row(i).dot(B) != 0))
+        den = sp.ilcm(*[value.q for value in witness])
+        witness *= den
+        gcd = sp.igcd(*[abs(int(value)) for value in witness if value])
+        witness /= gcd
+        assert C.T * witness == sp.zeros(C.cols, 1)
+        assert witness.dot(B) != 0
+        out = {
+            "n": N, "block_size": R, "sz_zero_dimension": len(ZERO),
+            "columns": C.cols, "rank": rank, "augmented_rank": augmented_rank,
+            "witness_dot_source": str(witness.dot(B)),
+            "witness_nonzero_entries": sum(bool(v) for v in witness),
+            "witness_by_basis_word": {''.join('+' if s == 0 else '0' if s == 1 else '-' for s in w): str(witness[i])
+                                      for i, w in enumerate(ZERO) if witness[i]},
+        }
+        path = Path(__file__).with_name('aklt_r3_obstruction.json')
+        path.write_text(json.dumps(out, indent=2) + '\n')
+        print(json.dumps({k: v for k, v in out.items() if k != 'witness_by_basis_word'}, indent=2))
+
+    both_cols = [col for j in range(N)
+                 for placement in (0, -1)
+                 for col in columns_for_bond(j, placement)]
+    both = sp.Matrix.hstack(*both_cols)
+    both_rank = DomainMatrix.from_Matrix(both).to_field().rank()
+    both_augmented_rank = DomainMatrix.from_Matrix(both.row_join(B)).to_field().rank()
+    both_out = {
+        "n": N, "block_size": R, "placements": ["right", "left"],
+        "sz_zero_dimension": len(ZERO), "columns": both.cols,
+        "rank": both_rank, "augmented_rank": both_augmented_rank,
+        "source_exactly_feasible": both_rank == both_augmented_rank,
+        "note": "Rank membership only; placement columns overlap within each physical bond, so their raw coefficient norm is not a dual upper bound.",
+    }
+    both_path = Path(__file__).with_name(f'aklt_r3_all_placements_n{N}.json')
+    both_path.write_text(json.dumps(both_out, indent=2) + '\n')
+    print(json.dumps(both_out, indent=2))
+
+
+if __name__ == '__main__':
+    main()

# Pressure access, sealing and useful repair are distinct operations
+
+Internal derivation, 14 October 2026. No alloy constitutive law was acquired.
+
+The selected task is durable repair of fatigue-relevant surface-connected pores in additive-manufactured metal, including pores whose narrow connecting path is unresolved by CT. The action is choosing a physically achievable repair process. The missing information is pressure-gas access and the evolving hot throat/bond state, not merely a reconstructed room-temperature pore shape.
+
+## Conservation before and after sealing
+
+Under ideal-gas, cylindrical, continuum, no-slip, quasi-steady, common-temperature assumptions, let external and internal absolute pressures be P and p, cavity volume V, throat radius a and length L, gas temperature T and viscosity mu. Write n=pV/(RT). Then
+
+    dn/dt = pi a^4 (P^2-p^2)/(16 mu L R T)
+    dp/dt = C(P^2-p^2) + p(T'/T - V'/V)
+    C = pi a^4/(16 mu L V).
+
+For q=p/P, c=-V'/V, theta=T'/T and r=P'/P,
+
+    q' = CP(1-q^2) + (c+theta-r)q.
+
+Shrinking the cavity and heating its gas increase internal pressure. Narrowing the throat decreases gas conductance. Neither effect can be dropped silently. These equations are conditional fluid mechanics, not a new physical law. Slip/Knudsen flow, nonideal gas, evolving complex throats, adsorption and gas dissolution require different or measured transport laws.
+
+After a genuinely gas-tight seal and with no dissolution/diffusion, n is fixed. At prescribed final temperature, p_f=p_s(V_s/V_f)(T_f/T_s). Without capillary or other closing traction, ongoing pressure-driven contraction to V_f requires
+
+    p_s/P_f <= (V_f/V_s)(T_s/T_f).
+
+If additional inward traction is bounded by Pi_max, replace P_f with P_f+Pi_max. This is a necessary quasistatic pressure-balance gate, not a universal volume floor in the presence of capillarity, plastic overshoot, gas loss or bonding. An adiabatic sealed gas has a different relation, pV^gamma=constant. CT disappearance alone does not establish a seal, diffusion bond, fatigue improvement or absence of regrowth.
+
+## A conservative pressure-slew exclusion certificate
+
+Suppose P>=0 is nondecreasing and absolutely continuous, P'<=R_max, p>=0, C(t)>=C_min>0, and c+theta>=0 on an acquired interval. Let Delta=P-p with Delta(0)<=D. At a putative first crossing Delta=D, necessarily P>=D and
+
+    Delta' = P' - C D(2P-D) - (c+theta)p
+           <= R_max - C_min D^2.
+
+Hence, by scalar comparison (or a strict barrier followed by a limit), if R_max<=C_min D^2, Delta(t)<=D throughout the interval. In general Delta<=max{Delta(0),sqrt(R_max/C_min)}. This excludes attaining a declared minimum pressure deficit if the coefficient bound remains valid. It does NOT rule out arbitrarily slow below-threshold creep or independent capillary/chemical sealing. If a throat law has no deformation below an independently measured threshold Y>D, it excludes pressure-induced throat sealing over that interval. If a finite-time creep upper bound is instead supplied, integrate that upper bound and compare with the required closure strain. A throat may reduce C as it closes; an initial C alone is insufficient for the certificate.

+The fourth-root critical-radius expression under constant geometry is
+
+    a_critical = [16 mu L V R_max/(pi D^2)]^(1/4).
+
+With fixed acquired geometry, a>=a_critical makes the slew bound at most D (provided the initial deficit is at most D). It is a sensitivity expression, not a numerical prediction for an alloy. +
+For a fixed cavity, constant external step P_x, initial p=0 and fixed coefficient C_x,

# Direct hot-process gas provenance: construction and decisive limits
+
+The desired decision is whether to change printing/gas preparation, seal an accessible pore before HIP, or change the pressure/thermal process. Ordinary endpoint CT and total retained argon need not distinguish gas present before HIP from gas admitted during HIP. The proposed additional physical query is to use a calibrated stable-isotope argon composition during a small-coupon HIP trial, then extract gas from a CT-registered cavity under vacuum and measure total moles and isotope composition. It directly tests hot-process source rather than extrapolating a cold Xe/He transient.
+
+This is a **proposed diagnostic experiment**, not an acquired operation or a demonstrated repair. Generic isotope-tagged HIP gas, inert isotopes trapped in microporosities, and post-treatment mass-spectrometric readout are explicitly disclosed in EP3243585A1 (2016 priority; https://patents.google.com/patent/EP3243585A1/en, description around isotope-coded HIP and its argon table). Root inspected this primary patent. Its purpose is component authentication; it still preempts a generic new-operation claim. Individual fluid-inclusion noble-gas laser extraction/MS is established in minerals (Boehlke and Irwin 1992, DOI 10.1016/0016-7037(92)90126-4). Neither source establishes CT-registered single-micropore extraction and process control in an AM metal after HIP.
+
+## Exact consequence of the simplest source query
+
+Let f0 and fH be effective isotope fractions of retained pre-HIP and HIP-source argon, and let lambda be the fraction of retained gas originating in the HIP source. A calibrated two-source model gives f=(1-lambda)f0+lambda fH and lambda=(f-f0)/(fH-f0). This requires acquired endmember ranges that include fractionation, instrument mass bias, collection efficiency, initial-gas variation and any preferential loss. Bounds can be obtained by interval inversion; if the effective source ranges overlap or are unacquired, the implementation returns UNKNOWN.
+
+This identifies a **retained source fraction**. Isotopic counter-diffusion can replace original argon without adding net total gas. Therefore lambda is neither cumulative total ingress nor a seal time. Matrix/surface isotope uptake can also contaminate a pore extraction; blank subtraction and extraction localization are decisive physical calibrations. A positive source-specific isotope excess beyond all acquired blanks proves source atoms reached the sampled region; it does not alone prove a specific throat path or gas-tight bonding. A null signal requires an acquired sensitivity and open-path transport lower bound to rule out access.
+
+The synthetic interval test in isotope_query.py is reproducible, and an ordinary isotope-mixture decoder given identical measurements obtains exactly the same answer. There is no claimed algorithmic advantage. Any future contribution must be the physical query and its action-level validation or a material-specific resource advantage.
+
+## Why three argon isotopes do not give a general closure clock
+
+Even under favorable monotone no-outflow ingress, isotope counts are integrals y_i=integral f_i(t)dmu(t), with f36+f38+f40=1. They give total mass and at most two independent time functionals. For the physically admissible code f36=t/3, f38=t^2/3, f40=1-t/3-t^2/3 on [0,1], the positive measures
+
+    mu_A=(4/7) delta_(1/4)+(3/7) delta_(5/6)
+    mu_B=(1/6) delta_0+(2/3) delta_(1/2)+(1/6) delta_1
+
+have identical total mass, first moment 1/2, second moment 1/3 and all three isotope counts, but different last ingress times 5/6 and 1. Exact rational execution verifies this. No decoder can distinguish these model histories from those observations.
+
+An even simpler exchange adversary holds total moles constant. After a marker switch at t=1, let x'=k(t)(1-x). k=1 until cutoff 2 and k=1/2 until cutoff 3 give the same final x=1-exp(-1). The isotope endpoint reports integrated exchange, not the cutoff. Finite bins with three independent compositions can yield three bin masses only under a validated transport model and independently handled initial inventory. A small enrichment epsilon amplifies isotope count and blank errors by order 1/epsilon. No late-bin uptake bounds a seal time only if an open throat has a separately validated positive hot uptake rate under the challenge.
+
+## A physically bounded first test
+
+Use sparse engineered cavities on sacrificial coupons from one alloy/build, including independently known sealed, open, and throttled controls. Begin with a constant isotope composition for the whole cycle to avoid an unacquired fast gas-switching interface. Measure actual gas composition, pressure and temperature at the sample; quantify pre-existing argon, dead-volume carryover, surface/matrix uptake, extraction yield, vacuum blank, isotope discrimination and detector linearity. CT registration and blind sequential extraction must show that a single chosen cavity's gas can be separated from neighboring pores and the surrounding metal. Recovered isotope/mole balances must agree with known seeded standards before inferring source fractions in unknown defects.
+
+For scale only, an ideal 10 um-radius cavity at 100 MPa and 1200 K contains about 4.2e-11 mol total gas, or 4.2e-13 mol marker at 1% fraction. These are calculated quantities, not actual trapped inventories or detection guarantees. Published mineral/noble-gas instruments motivate feasibility; metal-specific backgrounds, laser release, aliquot split, dynamic range and recovery remain unacquired. Destruction means this is a process-policy experiment on witness coupons, not a same-part online controller. Transfer to production parts requires separate held-out validation.
+
+After calibration, compare printing, standard gas-HIP, rapid gas forging, and verified full-surface pre-seal/HIP arms on matched initial defects. Match heat treatment, surface finish and specimen geometry. Measure source-resolved gas, independently sectioned bonding, post-heat pore regrowth and fatigue or functional leakage. Give the existing-method comparator identical gas/CT/assay observations. Charge isotope procurement and recovery, dedicated lines, blank/purge cycles, sacrificial coupons, CT, extraction/MS, vessel work/thermal time, seal/removal, failed runs and functional testing. No quotes, facility access, full resource advantage or physical outcomes were acquired here.
+
+Decision: abandon generic isotope coding as a novelty claim and exact seal-clock reconstruction. A source-resolved pore assay is a narrower metrology hypothesis worth testing only with an existing small-coupon facility and validated extraction standards; it does not yet establish the requested new scientific capability.
+

+The selected scientific task

+Repair fatigue-relevant defects in additively manufactured metal parts when a
+CT-visible pore may be sealed or connected to the surface through an unresolved
+throat. This matters for reliable complex metal components, including parts with
+internal channels where complete coating, machining and inspection are difficult.

+(2020, DOI 10.1016/j.addma.2020.101191) find connected/near-surface defects resist

+come with a complete pressure-ramp trace. Tammas-Williams et al. (2016, DOI
+10.1007/s11661-016-3429-3) already document sub-XCT connections and surface-pore

+can remain unbonded or regrow. These are established source findings, not ours.

+The action ambiguity is concrete: an apparently identical cavity can need only
+qualified HIP, or first need a gas-tight surface seal/encapsulation, a different

+1. Rapid pressure before gas entry: constructed, then preempted
+
+Root investigated a pressure ramp that collapses or seals a connected throat
+before the gas equalizes. Under explicitly stated ideal-gas, common-temperature,
+cylindrical, continuum, no-slip assumptions,
+
+  n=pV/(RT),
+  n'=pi a^4(P^2-p^2)/(16 mu L R T),
+  q'=CP(1-q^2)+(c+theta-r)q,
+  C=pi a^4/(16 mu L V), q=p/P,
+  c=-V'/V, theta=T'/T, r=P'/P.
+
+Cavity compression and heating increase internal pressure and cannot be omitted.
+The near-equilibrium filling time is 8 mu L V/(pi a^4 P), with no extra RT.
+Unmeasured throat radius causes a fourth-power uncertainty. Sensitivity examples
+with illustrative geometry/properties are preserved; none predicts an actual
+AM throat. Slip, rarefaction, real-gas behavior and hot property uncertainty are

+    np.array([[0, 0], [-1, 0]], dtype=object),
+)
+I2 = np.eye(2, dtype=object)
+E = sum((np.kron(a, a) for a in A), np.zeros((4, 4), dtype=object))
+MAG = (1, 0, -1)
+PAIR_BASIS = ((0, 0), (0, 1), (0, 2), (1, 2), (2, 2))
+V_BASIS = ((0, 1, 1), (0, 1, 2), (1, 1, 1), (1, 1, 2))
+Q6 = {
+    (0, 0): {(0, 0): 6},
+    (0, 1): {(0, 1): 3, (1, 0): 3},
+    (0, 2): {(0, 2): 1, (1, 1): 2, (2, 0): 1},
+    (1, 2): {(1, 2): 3, (2, 1): 3},
+    (2, 2): {(2, 2): 6},
+}
+
+
+@dataclass(frozen=True)
+class Defect:
+    sites: tuple[int, ...]
+    q6: dict[tuple[int, ...], int]
+    c: np.ndarray
+
+
+def dual(bond, offset, u, v):
+    sites = tuple((bond + offset + t) % N for t in range(3))
+    pair_pos = -offset
+    q6 = {}
+    for pair, coeff in Q6[u[pair_pos:pair_pos + 2]].items():
+        word = list(u)
+        word[pair_pos:pair_pos + 2] = pair
+        q6[tuple(word)] = coeff
+    c = A[v[0]] @ A[v[1]] @ A[v[2]]
+    return Defect(sites, q6, c)
+
+
+def source():
+    return (
+        Defect((0,), {(0,): 6}, A[0]),
+        Defect((0,), {(2,): -6}, A[2]),
+    )
+
+
+def local_basis(bond):
+    out = []
+    for offset in (0, -1):
+        for v in V_BASIS:
+            mv = sum(MAG[t] for t in v)
+            for pair in PAIR_BASIS:
+                for spectator in range(3):
+                    u = (*pair, spectator) if offset == 0 else (spectator, *pair)
+                    if sum(MAG[t] for t in u) == mv:
+                        out.append(dual(bond, offset, u, v))
+    assert len(out) == 24
+    return out
+
+
+def overlap(left, right):
+    """Exact overlap of *six-times-scaled* states via 4x4 transfers."""
+    if isinstance(left, tuple):
+        return sum(overlap(item, right) for item in left)
+    if isinstance(right, tuple):
+        return sum(overlap(left, item) for item in right)
+    lp = {site: p for p, site in enumerate(left.sites)}
+    rp = {site: p for p, site in enumerate(right.sites)}
+    total = 0
+    for lw, lc in left.q6.items():
+        for rw, rc in right.q6.items():
+            product = np.eye(4, dtype=object)
+            compatible = True
+            for site in range(N):
+                il = lp.get(site)
+                ir = rp.get(site)
+                if il is None and ir is None:
+                    transfer = E
+                elif il is not None and ir is not None:
+                    if lw[il] != rw[ir]:
+                        compatible = False
+                        break
+                    transfer = np.kron(left.c if il == 0 else I2,
+                                       right.c if ir == 0 else I2)
+                elif il is not None:
+                    transfer = np.kron(left.c if il == 0 else I2, A[lw[il]])
+                else:
+                    transfer = np.kron(A[rw[ir]], right.c if ir == 0 else I2)
+                product = product @ transfer
+            if compatible:
+                total += int(lc * rc * np.trace(product))
+    return total
+
+
+def exact_affine_solution(matrix, rhs):
+    reduced, pivots = DomainMatrix.from_Matrix(matrix.row_join(rhs)).to_field().rref()
+    if matrix.cols in pivots:
+        raise AssertionError("Gram normal equations inconsistent")
+    r = reduced.to_Matrix()
+    x = sp.zeros(matrix.cols, 1)
+    for row, col in enumerate(pivots):
+        x[col] = r[row, matrix.cols]
+    assert matrix * x == rhs
+    free = [j for j in range(matrix.cols) if j not in pivots]
+    null = sp.zeros(matrix.cols, len(free))
+    for k, j in enumerate(free):
+        null[j, k] = 1
+        for row, col in enumerate(pivots):
+            null[col, k] = -r[row, j]
+    assert matrix * null == sp.zeros(matrix.rows, len(free))
+    return x, null, len(pivots)
+
+
+def exact_solution(matrix, rhs):
+    x, null, rank = exact_affine_solution(matrix, rhs)
+    assert null.cols == 0 and rank == matrix.cols
+    return x
+
+
+def main():
+    base = local_basis(0)
+    kernels = []
+    for distance in range(3):
+        other = local_basis(distance)
+        block = np.array([[overlap(left, right) for right in other]
+                          for left in base], dtype=object)
+        kernels.append(block)
+    assert np.array_equal(kernels[0], kernels[0].T)
+    # A bond's left/right placements overlap; use independent columns from
+    # the exact same-bond Gram block before assigning a physical dual norm.
+    _, pivots = DomainMatrix.from_Matrix(sp.Matrix(kernels[0].tolist())).to_field().rref()
+    pivots = list(pivots)
+    assert len(pivots) == 20
+    local_dim = len(pivots)
+    blocks = [k[np.ix_(pivots, pivots)] for k in kernels]
+    for distance in range(3, N - 2):
+        assert overlap(base[0], local_basis(distance)[0]) == 0
+
+    dim = N * local_dim
+    k = np.zeros((dim, dim), dtype=object)
+    for j in range(N):
+        sl = slice(j * local_dim, (j + 1) * local_dim)
+        k[sl, sl] = blocks[0]
+        for distance in (1, 2):
+            l = (j + distance) % N
+            sr = slice(l * local_dim, (l + 1) * local_dim)
+            k[sl, sr] = blocks[distance]
+            k[sr, sl] = blocks[distance].T
+    assert np.array_equal(k, k.T)
+
+    g = np.zeros(dim, dtype=object)
+    for bond in (0, N - 1):
+        local = local_basis(bond)
+        for a, raw_col in enumerate(pivots):
+            g[bond * local_dim + a] = overlap(local[raw_col], source())
+    h = overlap(source(), source())
+    z = int(np.trace(np.linalg.matrix_power(E, N)))
+    assert h * 3 == 36 * z * 2
+
+    ks = sp.Matrix(k.tolist())
+    gs = sp.Matrix(g.tolist())
+    c0, null, gram_rank = exact_affine_solution(ks, gs)
+    residual = sp.Integer(h) - gs.dot(c0)
+    assert residual == 0
+
+    # Minimize the *physical* sum of squared bond vectors over all affine
+    # solutions. M is block diagonal because the primal row is each physical
+    # bond; the left/right local placements were already merged in K00.
+    m0 = sp.Matrix(blocks[0].tolist())
+    metric = sp.diag(*([m0] * N))
+    rref_numerator = (c0.T * metric * c0)[0]
+    correction = exact_solution(null.T * metric * null,
+                                -null.T * metric * c0)
+    c = c0 + null * correction
+    assert ks * c == gs
+    assert null.T * metric * c == sp.zeros(null.cols, 1)
+    numerator = (c.T * metric * c)[0]
+    assert numerator <= rref_numerator
+    upper = numerator / (36 * z)
+    rref_upper = rref_numerator / (36 * z)
+
+    output = {
+        "n": N,
+        "full_hilbert_dimension_not_built": 3**N,
+        "transfer_dimension": 4,
+        "raw_local_columns_per_bond": 24,
+        "independent_local_columns_per_bond": local_dim,
+        "global_gram_dimension": dim,
+        "gram_nonzero_bond_distances": [0, 1, 2],
+        "gram_rank": gram_rank,
+        "nullity": null.cols,
+        "ground_norm_integer_gauge": z,
+        "source_norm_normalized": str(sp.Rational(h, 36*z)),
+        "membership_residual_exact": str(residual),
+        "source_in_span": True,
+        "feasible_dual_upper_rref_exact": str(rref_upper),
+        "feasible_dual_upper_rref_decimal": str(sp.N(rref_upper, 12)),
+        "optimal_dual_upper_exact": str(upper),
+        "optimal_dual_upper_decimal": str(sp.N(upper, 12)),
+        "note": "The dual norm is minimized over the stated finite R3 local span with the correct per-physical-bond metric. All Gram data came from local 4x4 transfer contractions.",
+    }
+    path = Path(__file__).with_name(f'aklt_compact_gram_n{N}.json')
+    path.write_text(json.dumps(output, indent=2)+'\n')
+    print(json.dumps(output, indent=2))
+
+
+if __name__ == '__main__':
+    main()
+

ASTRA ULTRA — FRONTIER CAPABILITY GENESIS v0001
+14 October 2026
+
+Outcome: a compact, exactly verifiable quantum-response construction was developed
+and tested. An equally informed established competitor gives a tighter bound on
+the matched instance. No exceptionally consequential new scientific capability,
+historical novelty or complete-resource advantage has been established.
+Mission status: NOT_ACHIEVED. Research recommendation: REDESIGN.
+
+The strongest operation
+
+The selected scientific task is to certify a local static response of an
+interacting quantum system without reconstructing all excitations. For a supplied
+exact frustration-free parent Hamiltonian H=sum_j L_j^*L_j and exact MPS ground
+state psi, let b=(V-<V>)psi. The target is chi=<b,H^+b>/<psi,psi>, the negative
+second-order energy coefficient for a local perturbation lambda V.
+
+The construction searches for local tensor rows w_j with sum_j L_j^*w_j=b exactly.
+That identity supplies a rigorous upper sum_j||w_j||^2/<psi,psi>. An arbitrary
+primal vector supplies the familiar variational lower; their difference is exactly
+sum_j||w_j-L_j x||^2/<psi,psi>. The abstract primal/dual principle is old. The
+developed computational operation is exact completion, physical-row metric
+optimization and verification through compact MPS transfer contractions.
+
+Frustration-free annihilation makes the completion Gram block banded: sufficiently
+distant local defects have exactly zero overlap. It permits an O(N)-dimensional
+coefficient problem at fixed local width and MPS bond dimension. Rational
+contractions, exact rank tests and norm optimization have polynomial bit cost in
+N and encoded input length under those fixed-parameter assumptions. This is a
+conditional algorithm with UNKNOWN on failed membership; it is not a proof that
+fixed width always suffices or provides useful accuracy. The exact tensors are
+essential inputs, generated analytically here rather than measured from matter.
+
+What was actually established
+
+The test is the noncommuting periodic spin-1 AKLT Hamiltonian with analytic
+bond-dimension-two ground MPS and a one-site S_z source. Both three-site placements
+containing each bond are needed. Exact explicit-sector membership passes at
+N=6,7,8,9. Transfer-only exact completion passes at N=6,12,20. At N=20 the Gram is
+400 by400, rank317; the 3,486,784,401-dimensional Hilbert space is never constructed.
+That receipt comes from an earlier unoptimized RREF version and establishes
+membership, not an optimized norm or accuracy comparison.
+
+At N=6, independent explicit-sector and compact implementations return the same
+exact optimized upper 159740147/109636215. The exact six-step Krylov lower yields
+
+    1.450337335573352 <= chi <= 1.457001657709544.
+
+The interval is about0.4595% wide relative to its lower endpoint. An independent
+exact direct response reference is 287145511231/197956185875, approximately
+1.450550837609686. It is used for validation, not supplied to certificate selection.
+At N=12, exact240-by240 Gram algebra returns the optimized-within-ansatz upper
+627710130295322/439731204269175, approximately1.42748598280. No N12 lower or matched
+full-resource advantage is claimed. Root copy-first replays independently rerun
+the exact N6 interval, compact N6/N12 calculations, narrow obstruction, virtual
+identity and comparator; their precise receipts are in root/REPLAY_RECEIPTS.json.
+
+The decisive competitor
+
+An absent supplied gap is not a capability advantage when the same local
+projectors let a competitor acquire one cheaply. Exact rational LDL checks on an
+open four-spin patch prove B^2 >=(2/5)B. The established Knabe finite-size argument
+then proves H^2 >=(1/10)H for these periodic chains N>=6. The same six-step primal
+with this acquired gap gives the certified upper1.4537037411509957. Its interval
+width0.00336640557764 is smaller than our dual width0.00666432213619.
+
+This sufficient matched competitor defeats the claimed advantage on the tested
+instance. It uses the same Hamiltonian, source and primal, and includes actual
+gap acquisition instead of assuming an oracle. Stronger known gap methods may
+improve it further. The calculation is a comparison of rigorous widths; it is not
+a completed MPS wall-time/memory benchmark. The program does not claim to have
+implemented every best response solver. Exact finite-sector response is itself an
+additional strong comparator at these small sizes.
+
+Failures and corrections that must survive
+
+The right-placement-only ansatz fails exactly at N6 (rank71 vs augmented72), with a
+saved integer left-null witness dotting b to-3552. That does not refute the merged
+two-placement ansatz. Nearby-bond subsets fail; successful local-width rows still
+spread across the chain. An initial root probe incorrectly charged overlapping
+placements as separate physical rows and produced a spuriously halved norm; the
+probe was corrected before any reported exact certificate. Within-bond cross terms
+are now included in the metric. Old audit reports precede the transfer-only
+implementation; root/PRINCIPAL_DERIVATION.txt and CLAIM_LEDGER.json record the later
+evidence rather than silently editing those source reports.
+
+Centering b against one ground state does not ensure orthogonality to every
+ground vector. Exact dual feasibility establishes the necessary range condition;
+approximate feasibility does not. A small omitted component at energy epsilon
+can cost residual_squared/epsilon. A two-spin open-AKLT kernel counterexample and
+a pinned exclusion-chain example preserve those limitations. All-N AKLT
+feasibility, robustness to uncertain inputs and a useful source-specific
+advantage remain open. The virtual-current commutator and transfer eigenvalue
+-1/3 are exact but do not supply the missing parent-row peeling identity.
+
+Selection and alternative work
+
+Six Sol Max and25 Luna Max workers were used in this campaign: five complementary
+Sol leads each delegated four bounded independent screens, followed by one Sol
+and five Luna workers concentrated on quantum dual construction, proof,
+counterexamples, implementation, priority and synthesis. Counts describe
+allocation, not aggregate inference time or scientific evidence. The principal
+agent developed the central operation/representation, corrected the physical row
+metric, and acquired and proved the defeating finite-patch comparator.
+
+Molecular response had a fresh PySCF executable interface: H4 and asymmetric H6
+integrals, exact references and finite-field/selected-CI comparisons were actually
+generated. Response-aware SCI collides with existing LR-SCI/LR-SCI-PT and
+property-oriented selection. The strongest privileged result consumed the held-out
+FCI answer; it is not a usable algorithm. Rare-event acquisition used original
+Schlogl jump paths instead of supplying a rare transition matrix. Insufficient
+barrier exposure left the required rate unconstrained; prepared controls and real
+smFRET traces did not establish the missing decision/outcome. Weighted-ensemble,
+forward-flux and importance-sampling competitors remain substantial.
+
+Current experimental matter/energy/control papers were examined, including
+atomically buried CrSBr writing, NV readout, lithium extraction and a photonic
+nonlinear primitive. Existing physical successes do not supply the proposed
+functional coupling, complete device energy balance or a new computational
+advantage. Their exact unresolved interfaces are retained in worker reports.
+The independent foundational line recovered a pinned Euclidean stationary
+varifold manuscript from GitHub and exposed the curvature correction needed for
+a smooth-ambient extension. Availability and compilation are not correctness;
+the extension remains open and was not substituted for the failed main objective.
+
+Astra Capital was retrieved at ace0cfc4437fe91c20ccd24d69e0ee4bb335e871, with the
+unmerged draftPR83 allocations checked separately. N764 is close supplied-Hodge
+primal/dual capital; its acquisition boundary and sparse comparator remain
+relevant, but no theorem transfer is assumed. N768/N770, N752/N753 and N788/N790
+were screened with their precise interfaces. The three Pro directions were
+treated as complementary resources; thread read availability/status is recorded
+separately, and no unavailable or unreviewed Pro result is used as a premise.
+
+Priority, reach and investment
+
+The construction does not establish a new abstract duality. Complementary
+variational bounds, MPS Hylleraas and analytic/correction-vector response, local
+MPS/PEPS patch bounds, and finite-size gap criteria are prior art. Recent locally
+gapped response theory also blocks a generic “no global gap” novelty claim. The
+focused search did not locate an identical compact local-row upper, but priority
+remains UNKNOWN. Source-level comparison details and primary links are retained.
+
+The plausible technological reach is rigorous response computation for selected
+quantum materials/models if exact or robustly certified inputs, useful completion
+and matched advantage can be acquired. This campaign establishes none of that
+application reach, no physical control and no TypeI/II enabling operation.
+
+REDESIGN before major investment. Require a scientifically meaningful,
+nonintegrable source/input family where existing coercivity, response and SDP
+methods genuinely struggle; prove/implement the low-cost completion; then compare
+at matched accuracy, input acquisition, preparation, tensor width, bit cost,
+verification and failure rate. An irrelevant decoupled tiny-gap spectator is not
+evidence of advantage. An all-N AKLT theorem alone would deepen mathematics but
+would not rescue the defeated capability claim. Preserve the finite result and
+all failures rather than replacing the objective with an easier exact fixture.
+
+Versioning and publication
+
+The source packet is versioned in the Ultra repository. The installed molecular
+.venv, regenerated LaTeX builds and nested Git metadata are excluded; exact tracked
+public repository bytes are preserved in a plain pinned source snapshot. Source inputs,
+scripts, reports, raw accessed data/PDFs, dependency requirements and file hashes
+are retained according to SOURCE_MANIFEST.json. Package integrity/replay does not
+establish external review or novelty. Capital intake and actual Git publication
+are tracked separately in a publication receipt; this source report does not
+assert that a commit, shared PR or merge has already occurred.
